# PC: Harmony Patching

Canonical page: <https://bsmg.wiki/modding/pc/harmony-patching.html> · Harmony docs: <https://harmony.pardeike.net/articles/patching.html>

Harmony lets a mod run code around, instead of, or inside a game method without editing the game files. It is the primary tool for altering behavior in PC Beat Saber.

## Setup

```csharp
using HarmonyLib;

internal class Plugin
{
    private Harmony harmony = null!;
    private static readonly Assembly ExecutingAssembly = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly();

    [Init]
    public Plugin(PluginMetadata metadata) => harmony = new Harmony(metadata.Id);

    [OnStart]
    public void OnApplicationStart() => harmony.PatchAll(ExecutingAssembly);

    [OnExit]
    public void OnApplicationQuit() => harmony.UnpatchSelf();
}
```

Use the plugin ID as the Harmony instance ID. `PatchAll` applies every class in the assembly carrying `[HarmonyPatch]`. For fine control, use `harmony.Patch(original, prefix, postfix, transpiler)`.

## Patch types

| Type | Runs | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prefix | Before the original | Gate execution (`return false` skips it), validate args, capture state, replace results |
| Postfix | After the original | Observe completion, read/replace `__result`, attach components |
| Transpiler | Compiles into the original IL | Rewriting internals that have no hook point |
| Finalizer | After the original, including exceptions | Cleanup or exception suppression |

Prefer postfix → prefix → transpiler, in that order. Transpilers are brittle across game updates and hard to review.

## Basic patches

```csharp
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(NoteController), nameof(NoteController.Init))]
internal class NoteInitPatch
{
    internal static void Postfix(NoteController __instance) =>
        Plugin.Log.Info($"A {__instance.GetType().Name} was initialized.");
}
```

```csharp
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(FlyingScoreEffect), nameof(FlyingScoreEffect.RefreshScore))]
internal class MaxScoreTextPatch
{
    internal static bool Prefix(FlyingScoreEffect __instance, int score, int maxPossibleCutScore)
    {
        if (score < maxPossibleCutScore)
            return true; // run the original

        __instance._text.text = "Hello World!";
        __instance._colorAMultiplier = 1f;
        return false; // skip the original
    }
}
```

`nameof` is safer than a string. When overloads exist, disambiguate with explicit argument types:

```csharp
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(SomeType), nameof(SomeType.DoThing), new[] { typeof(int), typeof(float) })]
```

Or use `[HarmonyPatch(typeof(T), "Method", MethodType.Getter)]` for property getters and `MethodType.Constructor` for constructors.

## Injected parameters

| Name | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `__instance` | declaring type | The target object (missing on static methods) |
| `___fieldName` | field type | Private field value; assignable |
| `__result` | return type | Return value; writable in postfixes |
| `__state` | any type | Value passed from prefix to postfix |
| `__originalMethod` | `MethodBase` | The patched method |
| `__args` | `object[]` | All arguments; writable, but slow |
| `__runOriginal` | `bool` | Whether the original runs (postfix/finalizer) |

Prefer direct named arguments (`int score`) over `__args`. Use `__state` instead of stashing data in static fields.

## Accessing private members

### Publicizer (preferred)

Mark the game assembly reference with `Publicize="true"` (see [project-setup.md](project-setup.md)). Private and protected members become accessible at compile time, with no runtime cost.

It cannot set `readonly` fields or getter-only auto-properties. For those, use reflection.

### Reflection

```csharp
using IPA.Utilities;

// Writes private fields, including readonly ones.
someObject.SetField("someValue", 0.5f);
```

For reads in hot paths, cache an accessor:

```csharp
private static readonly FieldAccessor<SomeClass, float>.Accessor SomeValueAccessor =
    FieldAccessor<SomeClass, float>.GetAccessor("someValue");

SomeValueAccessor(ref instance) = 1f;
```

For general private member access, prefer the publicizer. `ReflectionUtil` also exposes property setters and method invocation, but their generic signatures require explicit type arguments; check the BSIPA source before use.

Never publicize another mod's assembly. Use reflection, or request an API change.

## Patch classes and lifecycle

- A patch class can hold multiple patch methods.
- Static patch methods are the norm. For DI, use SiraUtil's [Affinity API](zenject-sirautil.md#affinity-patching).
- Patches are applied when `PatchAll` runs. Installing them in `[OnStart]` is standard; do not patch before the game's assemblies are loaded.
- `UnpatchSelf()` on exit prevents leaks across internal restarts.
- Patch priority: `[HarmonyPriority(Priority.High)]` when another mod may also patch the same method. Document any priority you set.

## Practical recipes

### Event-style postfix

```csharp
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(ScoreController), nameof(ScoreController.Start))]
internal class ScoreControllerStartPatch
{
    internal static void Postfix(ScoreController __instance) =>
        __instance.noteWasCutEvent += HandleNoteCut;

    private static void HandleNoteCut(NoteController note, NoteCutInfo info) { /* ... */ }
}
```

Remember to unsubscribe when the object is destroyed, or subscribe per-instance and let the object die with the event.

### Prefix with state

```csharp
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(SomeController), "HandleThing")]
internal class HandleThingPatch
{
    internal static void Prefix(out float __state, SomeController __instance) =>
        __state = __instance.Speed;

    internal static void Postfix(SomeController __instance, float __state, ref float __result) =>
        __result *= __state > 1f ? 2f : 1f;
}
```

### Guard a method entirely

```csharp
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(PlayerData), nameof(PlayerData.Save))]
internal class BlockSavePatch
{
    internal static bool Prefix() => !PluginConfig.Instance.DisableSaving;
}
```

### Patching coroutines and async

The visible method only starts the state machine. To affect per-frame behavior, patch the compiler-generated `MoveNext`:

```csharp
// Type name comes from the decompiler; the generated state machine is what runs each frame.
[HarmonyPatch(typeof(SomeController.<SomeCoroutine>d__12), "MoveNext")]
internal class SomeCoroutineMoveNextPatch
{
    internal static void Postfix(SomeController.<SomeCoroutine>d__12 __instance) { /* per-frame work */ }
}
```

Inspect the decompiler for the generated type name; it changes when the method changes. Use this sparingly.

## Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Consequence | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String method names | Silent no-op after a rename | `nameof`, or verify in ILSpy |
| Ambiguous overload | Wrong method patched | Pass explicit argument types |
| Throwing inside a patch | Breaks the game method and may crash | Wrap risky work in `try/catch`, log, and return the original path |
| Patching every frame with reflection | Frame drops | Cache `FieldAccessor`/delegates |
| Patching `Awake` from a mod that loads late | Never applied | Choose a hook point that runs after mod load |
| Assuming `__instance` exists | NullReference on static targets | Check the signature |
| Modifying `__result` in a prefix | Overwritten by the original | Change it in a postfix, or skip the original |
| Leaving patches installed on scene reload | Duplicate handlers | Unpatch on exit; remove event handlers |
| Transpiler assumptions | Breaks on game updates | Prefer prefix/postfix; add defensive matching |

## Verifying a patch

1. Confirm the class appears in the IPA console with `--verbose` and `--debug`.
2. Add a one-time log in the patch to prove invocation.
3. If nothing logs, verify the method signature in ILSpy and check that `PatchAll` ran after the assembly loaded.
4. Look for Harmony warnings in the log; failed patches usually produce an exception or a "patch not applied" message.

# PC: Install, Update, and Downgrade Mods

Canonical pages: <https://bsmg.wiki/pc-modding.html>, <https://bsmg.wiki/support/>

## Requirements

- Own Beat Saber on Steam or Oculus PC. Cross-buy from Quest gives you the Oculus PC copy.
- Run the game at least once before modding, including after a reinstall.
- The latest game version may not be moddable. Check `#modding-announcements` in the BSMG Discord before troubleshooting.

## Safe practice

- Beat Saber **never** requests Administrator. A UAC prompt after installing a mod means the mod is malicious. Do not accept; report it.
- Unverified mods from Discord channels carry risk. Prefer BeatMods through an installer.
- Avoid video tutorials; they are frequently outdated. The wiki is canonical.
- Back up `Beat Saber_Data\CustomLevels` periodically. Updates can reset it.

## Installers

| Tool | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [BSManager](https://bsmanager.io) | **Recommended** | Manages versions, mods, maps, and playlists. Can downgrade. Supports OneClick map installs. |
| [BeatSaberModManager](https://github.com/affederaffe/BeatSaberModManager/releases/latest) | Supported | Windows and Linux, BeatMods-backed. |
| [ModAssistant](https://github.com/bsmg/ModAssistant/releases/latest) | Legacy | No longer recommended; known bugs. |

All of them install BSIPA and mods into a selected game instance. BSManager is also the cleanest way to keep a separate modded instance per game version.

## Install folders

| Source | Default path |
| --- | --- |
| Steam | `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Beat Saber\` |
| Oculus | `C:\Program Files\Oculus\Software\Software\hyperbolic-magnetism-beat-saber\` |
| BSManager | `C:\Users\<user>\BSManager\BSInstances\` |
| Steam (other drive) | `F:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Beat Saber\` |
| Oculus (other drive) | `F:\Oculus\Software\Software\hyperbolic-magnetism-beat-saber\` |

The relevant subfolders are `Plugins` (mod DLLs), `Beat Saber_Data\Managed` (game assemblies), `Beat Saber_Data\CustomLevels` (songs), and `Playlists`.

## Manual installation

Only needed for mods that are not in an installer. A patched game already has BSIPA.

1. Run the game once.
2. Download BSIPA matching the game version from <https://github.com/bsmg/BeatSaber-IPA-Reloaded/releases>.
3. Extract its contents into the install folder so `IPA.exe`, `Libs`, and `winhttp.dll` sit next to `Beat Saber.exe`.
4. Run `IPA.exe` once to patch. The folder should now contain `IPA.exe`, `Libs`, `Plugins`, and the patched executable state.
5. Drop mod zips into the install folder, preserving their internal structure, or copy DLLs into `Plugins`. Install dependencies too.
6. Launch with `--verbose` to confirm plugins load.

If step 4 reports errors, BSIPA was not extracted to the correct level.

## Downgrading

### BSManager (Steam and Oculus)

Install the target version as a separate instance and mod that instance. This is the least destructive option and keeps the current install intact.

### Legacy branches (Steam)

1. Uninstall BSIPA in the installer. On 1.30+, uninstall all mods instead.
2. Steam → right-click Beat Saber → Properties → Betas.
3. Select `legacy1.40.8_unity_v2021.3.16f1`, `legacy1.37.1_unity_v2021.3.16f1`, `1.34.2_legacy`, or `legacy1.29.1_unity_ver2019.4.28f1`.
4. Let the download finish, run the game once, then re-mod.

### Legacy branches (Oculus)

1. Uninstall BSIPA (or all mods on 1.30+).
2. Open the Beat Saber store page → `Versions + Release Notes` → click `(LIVE)` next to the version.
3. Select the legacy branch, let it download, run the game once, then re-mod.

### OculusDowngrader

Alternative for Oculus installs: <https://computerelite.github.io/tools/Oculus/OculusDowngraderGuide.html>.

## Songs and playlists

- **In-game downloader:** `BetterSongSearch` (button may read `BETTERSONGSEARCH`) or `BeatSaverDownloader` (`MORE SONGS`) under the `MODS` menu.
- **Manual:** unzip a map so the folder contains `Info.dat`, `song.ogg`, and difficulty files, then place it in `Beat Saber_Data\CustomLevels`. One folder per map.
- **OneClick:** enable it in BSManager; clicking a BeatSaver map installs it directly.
- **Playlists:** install `PlaylistManager`, then either use BSManager's Maps tab or place `.bplist` files in `Beat Saber/Playlists` and hit download-all in-game.
- **SongCore** is strongly recommended even for vanilla custom songs: faster loading and the foundation for downloaders, leaderboards, and playlists.

## Uninstalling mods

- Installer-managed: select the version in BSManager → `Mods` tab → trash icon.
- Manual: delete the DLL from `Plugins`. Remove leftover config files from `UserData` if the mod stores them there.
- To fully un-mod: verify the game files to restore replaced binaries, then delete `Plugins`, `Libs`, `IPA.exe`, `winhttp.dll`, and any leftover `UserData` entries. A clean reinstall is simpler if the install is heavily modified.

## When a game update breaks mods

1. Do not reinstall mods immediately. Wait for BSIPA and core mods to publish builds for the new version.
2. Check `#modding-announcements`.
3. If the user needs to play now, downgrade to the last moddable version and mod that instance.
4. Never copy old `Plugins` into a new version and expect stability.

## Support triage

1. Get the IPA log (`--verbose`) and the game version.
2. Confirm the mod list matches that version.
3. Test with only core mods (BSIPA + SongCore + the mod under investigation).
4. Verify game files, then do a clean install if the managed folder is polluted.
5. Check <https://bsmg.wiki/support/> for the specific symptom before guessing.

## First build

Set the Beat Saber directory when prompted and enable "store this folder in config". Then build once before editing code. A successful build proves references resolve. With the MCP server, run `bsmt inspect .` or the `inspect_project` tool first; `build_mod` returns the same missing-reference diagnostics. If it fails:

- Re-select the game directory via `Tools` → `BSMT Project Tools`.
- Restart the IDE.
- Manually add references: `Dependencies` → `Add Beat Saber assembly references`, or reference DLLs from `Beat Saber_Data\Managed`.

## Project files

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `<Name>.csproj` | Build configuration and references. |
| `<Name>.csproj.user` | Local Beat Saber path, managed by BSMT or `bsmt setup`. Do not commit. |
| `Plugin.cs` | BSIPA entry point. |
| `Directory.Build.props` | Manifest metadata and dependency declarations. |
| `manifest.json` | Generated at build into the assembly; do not hand-edit. |

## `Directory.Build.props`

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <PluginId>MyMod</PluginId>
  <PluginName>MyMod</PluginName>
  <Authors>YourName</Authors>
  <Version>1.0.0</Version>
  <GameVersion>1.40.8</GameVersion>
  <Description>Short description of what the mod does.</Description>

  <!-- optional -->
  <ProjectSource>https://github.com/you/MyMod</ProjectSource>
  <ProjectHome>https://example.com</ProjectHome>
  <Donate>https://ko-fi.com/you</Donate>
  <PluginIcon>icon.png</PluginIcon>
</PropertyGroup>

<ItemGroup>
  <DependsOn Include="BSIPA" Version="4.3.7" />
  <DependsOn Include="BeatSaberMarkupLanguage" Version="1.14.2" />
  <DependsOn Include="SiraUtil" Version="3.4.0" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Rules:

- Keep the `BSIPA` dependency; BSIPA requires it.
- Give every dependency a `Version`. `setup-beat-saber` in CI skips dependencies without one, and it reads the value as npm semver (`4.3.7`, `^4.3.6`), not a NuGet bracket range.
- `PluginId` and `PluginName` should be identical and space-free for BeatMods uploads.
- `Version` follows SemVer.
- `GameVersion` must exactly match the game build you compile against.
- Add `ConflictsWith`, `LoadAfter`, or `LoadBefore` when load order matters.
- Add `RequiredFile` for external libraries shipped alongside the DLL.
- Use `PluginHint` if `Plugin.cs` is moved.

## References

Reference game assemblies from `Beat Saber_Data\Managed` with `Private=false` so they are not copied into the output:

```xml
<Reference Include="Main">
  <HintPath>$(BeatSaberDir)\Beat Saber_Data\Managed\Main.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Add `SiraUtil`, `Zenject`, and `Zenject-usage` when using dependency injection. Add BSML when building UI.

### Publicizing game assemblies

Install `BepInEx.AssemblyPublicizer.MSBuild` and mark the reference:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="BepInEx.AssemblyPublicizer.MSBuild" Version="0.4.2">
  <PrivateAssets>all</PrivateAssets>
  <IncludeAssets>runtime; build; native; contentfiles; analyzers; buildtransitive</IncludeAssets>
</PackageReference>

<Reference Include="Main" Publicize="true">
  <HintPath>$(BeatSaberDir)\Beat Saber_Data\Managed\Main.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Never publicize another mod's assembly. Use reflection or ask the maintainer.

## Build outputs

- Debug and Release builds copy the DLL into `<BeatSaberDir>\Plugins`.
- Release additionally produces a distributable zip at `bin\Release\net472\zip\`.

## Config

BSIPA's `Config` provider generates a strongly typed config object backed by `UserData/<PluginId>.json`:

```csharp
[Init]
public Plugin(Logger logger, Config config)
{
    Log = logger;
    PluginConfig.Instance = config.GenerateConfigObject<PluginConfig>();
}
```

Guidelines:

- Use `public virtual` properties so the generated subclass can intercept changes.
- Add `[NotifyPropertyChanges]` on the config class if you need `INotifyPropertyChanged`.
- Use `[SerializedName("old_name")]` to rename a property without losing existing values.
- Do not use fields; use properties.
- Treat the config object as global state: `PluginConfig.Instance` is set once in `[Init]`.

# PC: Release and Support

Canonical pages: <https://bsmg.wiki/modding/pc/>, <https://bsmg.wiki/support/> · BeatMods: <https://beatmods.com>

## Pre-release checklist

- [ ] `PluginId`, `PluginName`, `Authors`, `Version`, `GameVersion`, `Description` are correct in `Directory.Build.props`.
- [ ] Dependencies are declared and version-compatible.
- [ ] `PluginId` and `PluginName` match and contain no spaces.
- [ ] Mod builds in `Release`, not just `Debug`.
- [ ] Tested with `--verbose`, in every affected mode.
- [ ] Tested through an internal restart.
- [ ] Tested on a debug Unity player if the mod touches gameplay, Unity objects, or threading.
- [ ] No unhandled exceptions in the log during normal use.
- [ ] No per-frame logging, allocations, or `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll` in hot paths.
- [ ] Config defaults are sane and the mod works with no config file present.
- [ ] Uninstall leaves no broken state (patches removed, files optional).
- [ ] README explains what it does, requirements, install, and known conflicts.

## Release build

In BSMT, switch the build configuration to `Release`, then build. Outputs:

- DLL copied into the target `Plugins` folder.
- Distributable zip in `bin\Release\net472\zip\`.

Inspect the zip before publishing:

```text
MyMod.zip
└── Plugins/
    └── MyMod.dll
```

Ship dependencies only if they are not available in the mod repository. Declare them so the installer resolves them.

## BeatMods submission

BeatMods is the repository installers pull from. Review the current [approval guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15RBVesZdS-U94AvesJ2DJqcnAtgh9E2PZOcbjrQle5Y/edit) before submitting.

Practical expectations inferred from the guidelines and wiki:

- The mod must work on the declared game version.
- No exceptions on a debug Unity build.
- Manifest metadata must be accurate and stable.
- Avoid bundling other mods' assemblies.
- Provide source or a contact path when asked.
- Accept that review can take time; respond to reviewer feedback.

Version bumps: patch for fixes, minor for features, major for breaking config or API changes.

## Automated builds and tag releases

GitHub Actions can build the mod on every push and attach the release zip to a tag automatically.

- Build workflow: checkout, `nicoco007/setup-beat-saber`, `dotnet build -c Release`, package `bin\Release\net472\Final` into a zip, upload it as an artifact.
- Release workflow: triggered by `push` of `v*` tags, builds the tagged commit, then creates a GitHub Release for that tag with the zip attached.
- `permissions: contents: write` is required for the release step.
- On GitHub Actions the standard BSMT props disable `ZipRelease`, so the workflow packages the `Final` folder rather than looking for `bin\Release\net472\zip`.

Full walkthrough, workflow files, version/tag synchronization, and troubleshooting: [automated-builds.md](automated-builds.md). Templates: [`../assets/workflows/build.yml.txt`](../assets/workflows/build.yml.txt) and [`../assets/workflows/release.yml.txt`](../assets/workflows/release.yml.txt).

Every `DependsOn` needs a `Version` in npm-semver form (`4.3.7`, `^4.3.6`); `setup-beat-saber` skips dependencies without one and selects the lowest matching version otherwise. See [dependency version syntax](automated-builds.md#dependency-version-syntax).

Tag flow:

```powershell
# after bumping Version in Directory.Build.props and merging
git tag v1.2.3
git push origin v1.2.3
```

Verify the release page after the workflow finishes: the tag should have the zip asset and generated notes.

## Distribution outside BeatMods

GitHub Releases is the normal path for beta builds and mods not yet accepted. Attach the BSMT zip and state the exact supported game version in the release notes.

## Supporting users

Ask for, in this order:

1. The exact game version and platform (Steam / Oculus / BSManager instance).
2. The full IPA log from a `--verbose` launch, not a screenshot of the last line.
3. Whether the issue happens with only core mods installed.
4. Steps to reproduce, including game mode.

Then:

- Reproduce locally on the same version.
- Check whether another mod patches the same method.
- If the game updated, confirm compatibility before debugging the mod itself.
- Close with a concrete fix or a clear "not supported on this version" statement.

Do not ask users to run as Administrator, disable antivirus globally, or install unverified DLLs.

## Maintaining across game updates

1. Watch `#modding-announcements`.
2. Update references, `GameVersion`, and dependency versions.
3. Rebuild and run the full test matrix.
4. Re-check patches that rely on signatures or IL — these break first.
5. Publish a version per supported game version; do not advertise a range you have not tested.

## Deprecation

If the mod is no longer maintained, say so in the README and release notes, archive the repository if appropriate, and remove or flag the BeatMods listing. Users should not be left guessing whether a crash is expected.

# Quest: BSML User Interfaces

Canonical page: <https://bsmg.wiki/modding/quest/ui.html> · Docs: <https://redbrumbler.github.io/Quest-BSML-Docs/>

Quest BSML provides two ways to build UI:

- **BSML-Lite** — C++ helpers that create components directly.
- **BSML XML** — `.bsml` resources parsed at runtime, closer to the PC workflow.

Lite is the common path for settings pages because it avoids embedding and parsing resources.

## Install

```powershell
qpm dependency add bsml
qpm dependency add custom-types
qpm restore
```

`custom-types` is required by BSML even if your mod does not declare its own types.

## Initialize

```cpp
#include "bsml/shared/BSML.hpp"

MOD_EXTERN_FUNC void late_load() noexcept {
    il2cpp_functions::Init();
    custom_types::Register::AutoRegister();
    BSML::Init();

    BSML::Register::RegisterMainMenuViewControllerMethod(
        "My Mod", "Settings for My Mod", "My Mod", DidActivate);

    // install hooks after registration
}
```

`BSML::Init()` must run after `il2cpp_functions::Init()` and before any registration.

## `DidActivate`

BSML calls your method when the page is shown:

```cpp
#include "bsml/shared/BSML.hpp"

void DidActivate(HMUI::ViewController* self, bool firstActivation,
                 bool addedToHierarchy, bool screenSystemEnabling) {
    if (!firstActivation) return;

    auto* container = BSML::Lite::CreateScrollableSettingsContainer(self->get_transform());
    BSML::Lite::CreateText(container->get_transform(), "Hello World!");
}
```

Rules:

- Create components only when `firstActivation` is true; otherwise they duplicate on every open.
- Use a container (`CreateScrollableSettingsContainer`, horizontal/vertical layouts) to control placement.
- Keep references to components you need to update later; the tree is rebuilt per activation.

## Registration points

| Location | Registration |
| --- | --- |
| Main menu view controller | `BSML::Register::RegisterMainMenuViewControllerMethod(title, buttonText, hoverHint, DidActivate)` |
| Mod settings | `BSML::Register::RegisterSettingsMenu(name, DidActivate, true)` |
| Gameplay setup | `BSML::Register::RegisterGameplaySetupTab(name, DidActivate)` with `void(GameObject* self, bool firstActivation)` |
| Left menu button | `BSML::Register::RegisterMenuButton(text, hoverHint, onClick)` |

The gameplay setup callback signature is `void(UnityEngine::GameObject* self, bool firstActivation)` — there is no view controller.

Registration APIs have changed across BSML versions. Check `extern/includes/bsml/shared/BSML.hpp` for the exact overloads in your build; the signatures above match current BSML.

## BSML-Lite components

| Helper | Produces |
| --- | --- |
| `CreateScrollableSettingsContainer(transform)` | Scroll view suitable for settings |
| `CreateVerticalLayoutGroup(transform, ...)` | Vertical stack |
| `CreateHorizontalLayoutGroup(transform, ...)` | Horizontal row |
| `CreateGridLayoutGroup(transform, ...)` | Grid |
| `CreateText(transform, "text", fontSize)` | Text label |
| `CreateUIButton(transform, "text", onClick)` | Button |
| `CreateToggle(transform, "label", value, onToggle)` | Toggle |
| `CreateSliderSetting(transform, "label", increment, value, min, max, onValueChange)` | Slider |
| `CreateIncrementSetting(transform, "label", ...)` | Increment/decrement control |
| `CreateStringSetting(transform, "label", value, onValueChange)` | Text input |
| `CreateDropdown(transform, ...)` | Dropdown |
| `CreateColorPicker(transform, ...)` | Color picker |
| `CreateProgressBar(transform, ...)` | Progress bar |
| `CreateFloatingScreen(...)` | World-space screen |

The `BSML-Lite/Creation` headers document nearly every helper and its overloads. Read them in `extern/includes/bsml/` rather than guessing.

### Wiring config values

```cpp
void DidActivate(HMUI::ViewController* self, bool firstActivation,
                 bool addedToHierarchy, bool screenSystemEnabling) {
    if (!firstActivation) return;

    auto* container = BSML::Lite::CreateScrollableSettingsContainer(self->get_transform());

    BSML::Lite::CreateToggle(container->get_transform(), "Enable feature",
        getModConfig().Enabled.GetValue(),
        [](bool value) { getModConfig().Enabled.SetValue(value); });

    BSML::Lite::CreateSliderSetting(container->get_transform(), "Volume",
        0.05f, getModConfig().Volume.GetValue(), 0.0f, 1.0f,
        [](float value) { getModConfig().Volume.SetValue(value); });
}
```

`SetValue` writes the config file. `CreateSliderSetting`'s `applyValueTime` argument defaults to 1 second, which limits write frequency; for other controls, debounce if the callback fires continuously.

## XML views

BSML also parses `.bsml` XML. The Quest docs list the supported tags and attributes:

- <https://redbrumbler.github.io/Quest-BSML-Docs/>
- Embed the resource, then load it through the BSML API for the target screen.

Use XML when porting a PC view or when the layout is complex. Use Lite for small settings pages — it is easier to debug without resource-path issues.

## Sizing and layout

- Default UI scale is small; use layout groups instead of absolute positions.
- `child-expand-height` / `child-control-height` behave differently than PC BSML. Check the Quest docs.
- Test in the actual headset. A layout that looks fine in a flat preview can be unreadable at VR distance.
- Avoid deep nesting; il2cpp UI creation is more expensive than on PC.

## Pitfalls

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nothing appears in the menu | `BSML::Init()` missing, or registration after hooks | Init first, register before installing hooks |
| Duplicate widgets | Components created when `firstActivation` is false | Guard with `firstActivation` |
| Crash in `CreateScrollableSettingsContainer` | Wrong parent transform or BSML not initialized | Pass `self->get_transform()`, check init order |
| Gameplay tab crashes | Used the view-controller signature | Use `void(GameObject*, bool)` |
| Text/toggle does not persist | Callback does not write config | Call `SetValue` in the callback |
| UI works once, then breaks after reopening | Stale component pointers | Rebuild on activation; do not cache Unity objects across scenes |
| Unresolved BSML symbols | Wrong BSML version for this game build | Install the BSML version matching the codegen |

# Quest: Build, Test, Debug

Canonical page: <https://bsmg.wiki/modding/quest/intro.html#testing-your-mod>

## Build and deploy

```powershell
qpm s build                 # compile only
qpm s copy                  # build, push to headset, restart the game
qpm s copy -log -self -file latest.log
qpm s restart               # restart without rebuilding
qpm s qmod                  # build an installable .qmod
```

`copy.ps1` pushes `build/lib<id>.so` to the modloader directory on the headset and restarts Beat Saber. Requires an authorized ADB device.

### ADB basics

```powershell
adb devices                 # must show "device", not "unauthorized"
adb shell                   # shell on the headset
adb logcat -c               # clear logs
adb logcat -s Unity         # Unity-tagged logs
adb pull /sdcard/Android/data/com.beatgames.beatsaber/files/tombstone_01 .
```

Put the headset on and accept the USB debugging prompt the first time. Close SideQuest if it holds the ADB connection.

## Logging

```powershell
qpm s logcat                # all Beat Saber output
qpm s logcat -self          # only your mod
qpm s logcat -self -file latest.log
```

Recommendations:

- `-self` makes your own hook output readable.
- Clear the buffer (`adb logcat -c`) before reproducing an issue so the trace is short.
- Do not log per frame in a build you intend to publish.
- If the game dies too fast to read the console, reproduce while `qpm s logcat -file crash.log` is running.

## Native crash triage

Beat Saber writes native crash tombstones on the device.

```powershell
qpm s tomb                  # pull the newest tombstone
qpm s tomb -analyze         # map frames to source when the build matches
qpm s stack                 # symbolicate
```

Tombstone location:

```text
/sdcard/Android/data/com.beatgames.beatsaber/files/tombstone_01
/sdcard/Android/data/com.beatgames.beatsaber/files/tombstone_02
...
```

The newest file has the highest suffix. `-analyze` only gives useful source lines when the deployed `.so` matches the local build exactly.

Reading a tombstone:

1. Find the first frame inside your mod (`lib<id>.so`), not the deepest framework frame.
2. Symbolicate with `ndk-stack` and the matching unstripped library.
3. If the crash is in a hook, the signature is usually wrong or a pointer is null.
4. If the crash is at load, check `AutoRegister`, static initialization order, and dependency versions.

## Test matrix

| Area | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Boot | Game reaches the main menu with the mod installed |
| Menu | Registered tabs/pages open, close, and reopen without duplication |
| Config | Values load, change, persist across a game restart |
| Gameplay | Hook behavior in Solo, Party, Campaign, and multiplayer if applicable |
| Scene changes | Enter/leave a map repeatedly; no stale pointers or duplicate coroutines |
| Multiple activations | Close and reopen menus; components rebuild correctly |
| Device | Test on the actual headset, not a flat preview |
| Packaging | Install the `.qmod` through MBF/QuestPatcher and boot |

## Common failures

| Symptom | Diagnose with | Likely fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Black screen then crash to home | tombstone | Hook signature, missing init, or bad dependency version |
| Game boots but mod log lines never appear | logcat, `Modloader` folder | Wrong `.so` name, mod not copied, Scotland2 not initialized |
| Hook fires but values are wrong | logcat + codegen | Wrong field or wrong overload |
| Crash only after opening a menu | logcat | UI built outside `firstActivation`, stale component pointer |
| Crash only after a restart | logcat | Custom type or coroutine not cleaned up |
| `adb: device unauthorized` | `adb devices` | Accept the prompt in the headset, reinstall ADB drivers |
| QMOD installs but does not load | `qpm s validate`, QMOD contents | `mod.json` mismatch, wrong `packageVersion`, missing mod file |

## Clean rebuild

```powershell
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force build
qpm restore
qpm s build
```

Delete `extern/` only if you suspect a corrupted restore; then `qpm restore` again.

## Pre-release test pass

1. Fresh install of the `.qmod` through MBF.
2. Boot to menu, open every UI page.
3. Play one map with the feature enabled and one with it disabled.
4. Change every config value, restart the game, verify persistence.
5. Uninstall and reinstall the mod; verify no stale config breaks it.
6. Check the log for warnings from your mod during the whole pass.

# Quest: Configuration with config-utils

Canonical page: <https://bsmg.wiki/modding/quest/config.html>

`config-utils` generates a typed config backed by a JSON file. Declare values once, initialize once, then get/set.

## Install

```powershell
qpm dependency add config-utils
qpm restore
```

`beatsaber-hook` already includes config-utils headers, but declare the dependency explicitly so QPM resolves it.

## Declare

`include/modconfig.hpp`:

```cpp
#pragma once

#include "config-utils/shared/config-utils.hpp"
#include "UnityEngine/Color.hpp"
#include "UnityEngine/Vector2.hpp"
#include "UnityEngine/Vector3.hpp"
#include "UnityEngine/Vector4.hpp"

DECLARE_CONFIG(ModConfig,
    CONFIG_VALUE(Enabled, bool, "Enabled", true);
    CONFIG_VALUE(Volume, float, "Volume", 0.8f);
    CONFIG_VALUE(Label, std::string, "Label", "default");
    CONFIG_VALUE(Count, int, "Count", 3);
    CONFIG_VALUE(Scale, double, "Scale", 0.5);
    CONFIG_VALUE(Tint, UnityEngine::Color, "Tint", UnityEngine::Color(1.0f, 0.5f, 0.0f, 1.0f));
    CONFIG_VALUE(Offset, UnityEngine::Vector2, "Offset", UnityEngine::Vector2(0, 0));
    CONFIG_VALUE(Position, UnityEngine::Vector3, "Position", UnityEngine::Vector3(0, 1, 2));
    CONFIG_VALUE(Bounds, UnityEngine::Vector4, "Bounds", UnityEngine::Vector4(1, 1, 1, 1));
)
```

`CONFIG_VALUE(Name, Type, "Display name", default)`

Supported types: `bool`, `int`, `float`, `double`, `std::string`, `UnityEngine::Color`, `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Vector4`.

`UnityEngine::Color` components are `0..1`, not `0..255`.

## Initialize

```cpp
#include "modconfig.hpp"

MOD_EXTERN_FUNC void late_load() noexcept {
    il2cpp_functions::Init();
    getModConfig().Init(modInfo);   // must run before any GetValue/SetValue
}
```

`Init` also loads the file from disk. Calling `GetValue` first crashes.

`modInfo` is the `modloader::ModInfo` defined in `main.cpp`.

## Read and write

```cpp
bool enabled = getModConfig().Enabled.GetValue();
getModConfig().Enabled.SetValue(true);          // saves the file immediately

auto color = getModConfig().Tint.GetValue();
color.a = 0.5f;
getModConfig().Tint.SetValue(color);
```

Every `SetValue` writes the JSON file. Do not call it per frame; batch changes or only write on user action.

## Where the file lives

```text
/sdcard/ModData/com.beatgames.beatsaber/Configs/<mod-id>.json
```

On a PC with ADB:

```powershell
adb pull /sdcard/ModData/com.beatgames.beatsaber/Configs/myquestmod.json
```

If values do not persist:

1. Confirm `Init` ran (add a log after it).
2. Confirm the mod ID is stable; changing it creates a new file.
3. Check that the config file is valid JSON; a corrupted file may fail to load.
4. Confirm the mod has write access to `ModData` (it should, under the default install).

## Common patterns

### Migrating a config

Add new values with defaults; existing files get the default on load. Do not rename values casually — the old key is simply ignored and users lose their setting. If a rename is necessary, read the old key once and write the new one.

### Thread safety

Config access is not a synchronization primitive. Read values on the main thread, or copy them into atomics when a hook runs on another thread.

### Sharing a config across source files

Include `modconfig.hpp`; `getModConfig()` returns the same static instance.

### Defaults that depend on runtime state

`CONFIG_VALUE` defaults must be compile-time constants. Compute the effective value at the point of use instead:

```cpp
float volume = getModConfig().Volume.GetValue() * getDefaultVolume();
```

## Pitfalls

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Crash at startup | `GetValue` before `Init` | Call `getModConfig().Init(modInfo)` in `late_load()` |
| Values reset every launch | Init failed or file is not writable | Log after `Init`, check the Configs folder |
| Wrong colors | `0..255` passed to `Color` | Divide by 255 |
| Stutter when changing a slider | `SetValue` every frame | Save on release, or use a debounce |
| Config not found for another mod | Wrong mod ID | Use the ID from that mod's `mod.json` |

```powershell
cmake --version

adb version
```

# Quest: Hooking with beatsaber-hook

Canonical page: <https://bsmg.wiki/modding/quest/intro.html#hooking> · beatsaber-hook: <https://github.com/QuestPackageManager/beatsaber-hook>

Hooking intercepts a game method so your code runs before, after, or instead of it. `beatsaber-hook` wraps il2cpp and thunk creation so a hook is a macro plus one install call.

## How types are named

`bs-cordl` generates headers under `extern/includes/codegen`. They mirror the C# namespaces:

```cpp
#include "GlobalNamespace/StandardLevelDetailViewController.hpp"  // C#: GlobalNamespace.StandardLevelDetailViewController
#include "HMUI/CurvedTextMeshPro.hpp"                              // C#: HMUI.CurvedTextMeshPro
#include "UnityEngine/UI/Button.hpp"                               // C#: UnityEngine.UI.Button
```

If you only own the Quest version, these headers are your decompiler. If you own the PC version, an ILSpy/dnSpy browse of the same game version is easier to read, but the generated names must still match the codegen.

## Install sequence

```cpp
MOD_EXTERN_FUNC void late_load() noexcept {
    il2cpp_functions::Init();   // required before any il2cpp/hook work

    PaperLogger.info("Installing hooks...");
    INSTALL_HOOK(PaperLogger, MyHook);
    PaperLogger.info("Installed all hooks!");
}
```

`setup()` is too early. Do not install hooks before `il2cpp_functions::Init()`.

## `MAKE_HOOK_MATCH`

```cpp
MAKE_HOOK_MATCH(HookName,
    &Namespace::Class::Method, ReturnType,
    Namespace::Class* self, /* original arguments... */) {

    HookName(self, /* arguments... */);   // call the original

    // your code
}
```

Macro arguments:

| Position | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Hook variable name |
| 2 | Pointer to the target method |
| 3 | Return type |
| 4 | Target instance pointer (`self`) |
| 5+ | The original parameter list, exactly |

The hook function **must** match the target signature. A mismatch corrupts the stack or crashes on install.

## Example: change the level-detail play button

```cpp
#include "GlobalNamespace/StandardLevelDetailView.hpp"
#include "GlobalNamespace/StandardLevelDetailViewController.hpp"
#include "UnityEngine/UI/Button.hpp"
#include "UnityEngine/GameObject.hpp"
#include "HMUI/CurvedTextMeshPro.hpp"

MAKE_HOOK_MATCH(LevelUIHook,
    &GlobalNamespace::StandardLevelDetailViewController::DidActivate, void,
    GlobalNamespace::StandardLevelDetailViewController* self,
    bool firstActivation, bool addedToHierarchy, bool screenSystemEnabling) {

    LevelUIHook(self, firstActivation, addedToHierarchy, screenSystemEnabling);

    auto* detailView = self->_standardLevelDetailView;
    auto* button = detailView->actionButton;
    auto* text = button->get_gameObject()->GetComponentInChildren<HMUI::CurvedTextMeshPro*>();
    text->set_text("Skill Issue");
}
```

Notes:

- Fields like `_standardLevelDetailView` are the generated names for private C# fields and are usually accessible without reflection.
- Unity accessors are `get_`/`set_` methods (`get_gameObject()`, `set_text(...)`).
- `auto*` is fine; explicit types make signatures easier to audit.

## Calling the original

- Call the original at the start for "postfix" behavior.
- Call it at the end for "prefix" behavior.
- Skip it to replace behavior entirely.
- Do not call it twice unless the game can tolerate duplicate side effects.

For non-void methods, return the original call or your replacement:

```cpp
MAKE_HOOK_MATCH(GetSpeedHook, &GlobalNamespace::SomeController::GetSpeed, float,
    GlobalNamespace::SomeController* self) {
    float speed = GetSpeedHook(self);
    return speed * 1.5f;   // replace with your own config-driven logic
}
```

## Static methods and constructors

- Static target: omit `self` and mirror only the original parameters.
- Constructor: target the generated `ctor` (verify the exact symbol in the codegen header). Constructor hooks are easy to get wrong; prefer hooking the method that constructs or initializes the object when possible.
- Generic methods and overloads: verify the exact instantiated signature in codegen; `MAKE_HOOK_MATCH` cannot infer it.

beatsaber-hook also offers match-by-offset and find-by-name macros for cases where the generated pointer is unavailable. Prefer `MAKE_HOOK_MATCH`; use the others only when you have verified the symbol and understand the version coupling.

## Hook ordering

- Multiple mods can hook the same method. The last installed hook becomes the entry point and calls the previous one through its trampoline, so behavior is order-dependent.
- Keep one hook per mod per method, and call the original exactly once.
- Avoid installing hooks conditionally on frame timing; do it in `late_load()`.

## Finding the right method

1. Search the codegen headers for the class (`grep -R "class SomeController" extern/includes/codegen`).
2. Read the method declaration and surrounding fields.
3. Cross-check behavior in a PC decompile of the same game version if available.
4. Log a unique string from the hook and confirm it appears with `qpm s logcat -self`.

## Crash and no-op causes

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| Game crashes immediately after installing the mod | Hook signature mismatch, or `INSTALL_HOOK` before `il2cpp_functions::Init()` |
| Hook never logs | Wrong method/overload, hook in `setup()` instead of `late_load()`, or codegen version mismatch |
| Crash when the hooked method runs | Null field access, wrong argument types, or calling the original with modified arguments of the wrong type |
| Works in one scene, crashes in another | The object or field does not exist in every mode/scene |
| Mod loads, but nothing changes | Another mod's hook replaces yours, or your replacement returns too early |

When a hook crashes, the tombstone is the fastest path to the faulting frame:

```powershell
qpm s tomb -analyze
qpm s stack
```

See [build-test-debug.md](build-test-debug.md).

## Safety rules

- Match the exact game version used for codegen.
- Validate every pointer before dereferencing; fields can be null during scene transitions.
- Do not allocate heavily or call Unity APIs off the main thread from a hook.
- Do not hook a method you cannot identify with certainty. A bad hook is a boot-loop.

# Quest: Install, Update, and Downgrade Mods

Canonical pages: <https://bsmg.wiki/quest-modding.html>, <https://bsmg.wiki/quest/modding-with-mbf.html>

## Before anything else

| Check | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Headset is Quest 1/2/3/3S/Pro standalone | Rift and Quest-via-Link use the PC workflow |
| Only one account on the headset | Multiple accounts block modding |
| Developer Mode is enabled | Required for ADB and patching |
| The user accepts the trade-offs | Modding disables official multiplayer and base-game leaderboards |
| Current game version is moddable | If not, downgrade during patching |

Custom leaderboards require `ScoreSaber` (<https://scoresaber.com/quest>) or `BeatLeader` (<https://beatleader.xyz>). Modded multiplayer requires `Beat Together` + `MultiplayerCore`, which may not be available on every version.

## Enable Developer Mode

1. Sign in at <https://developer.oculus.com/manage/organizations/create/> with the Meta account bound to the headset.
2. Enable 2FA; an organization cannot be created without it.
3. Create an organization (any name).
4. Open the Meta Quest phone app → headset settings → Developer Mode → enable.

## Back up save data

Modding normally preserves saves, but a backup is cheap:

1. Connect the headset to a PC.
2. In SideQuest (or any ADB file browser), open `sdcard/Android/data/com.beatgames.beatsaber/files`.
3. Copy `AvatarData.dat`, `PlayerData.dat`, and `settings.cfg` to the PC.

To restore, copy them back to the same path.

## ModsBeforeFriday (MBF)

MBF is the recommended tool. It runs in a Chromium browser (Edge/Chrome, **not** Firefox or Safari), downgrades to the latest moddable version, patches, and installs core mods.

1. Update the headset's Beat Saber to the current version (MBF downgrades as needed).
2. Open <https://lauriethefish.github.io/ModsBeforeFriday/> (mirror: <https://mbf.bsquest.xyz>).
3. Connect the headset by USB.
4. Click `Connect to Quest`, select the device, confirm the ADB prompt in the headset.
5. If prompted to downgrade, let MBF do it.
6. Click `Mod the app`. **Do not unplug during patching.**
7. After completion, use `Add Mods` to install additional mods from the built-in browser.

MBF installs a song downloader by default.

### Quest 1

Quest 1 can be patched to `1.40.8` only through MBF, because it needs a special compatibility patch. The last officially supported Quest 1 build is `1.37.101`. If MBF reports an unexpected version, make sure the headset is not on the legacy release channel:

1. Open the Beat Saber store page.
2. Sign in with the headset's account.
3. Find `Version + release notes`.
4. Select `LIVE`, reinstall Beat Saber, and retry.

## QuestPatcher

QuestPatcher is a desktop GUI for il2cpp Unity apps. It is useful when the connection is unstable or offline management is required.

- Download: <https://github.com/Lauriethefish/QuestPatcher/releases/latest>
- **It cannot downgrade Beat Saber.** Use it only when the installed version is already moddable.
- If it has been used before, run `Tools` → `Quick Fix` first.
- Select `Scotland2` as the mod loader when patching.
- Install core mods and extras from <https://mods.bsquest.xyz>.

## QAVS

QAVS cannot currently downgrade or patch Beat Saber correctly. Do not use it for patching; use MBF. Only follow <https://bsmg.wiki/quest/modding-with-qavs.html> if a knowledgeable source explicitly instructs it.

## BMBF

Deprecated and broken since the v63 update. It will not work. Do not attempt to mod with BMBF; migrate to MBF.

## Installing mods after patching

| Source | Use |
| --- | --- |
| MBF `Add Mods` | Easiest; resolves versions for the patched game |
| BSQMods <https://mods.bsquest.xyz> | Browse and download QMODs directly |
| QuestPatcher | Import a `.qmod` file manually |

QMODs are zip archives with a `mod.json` manifest. Side-loading a QMOD for the wrong game version can crash the game on boot.

## Updating the game

1. Do not accept a game update until the mods you need support it.
2. Back up saves.
3. Update, then patch again with MBF. MBF will downgrade if the new version is not moddable.
4. Reinstall mods for the new version; do not reuse old QMODs.

## Uninstalling mods

- MBF: remove mods from its mod list.
- QuestPatcher: select the mod and uninstall.
- Nuclear option: uninstall Beat Saber, reinstall, then patch again. Saves in `Android/data` are usually retained, but verify the backup first.

## Troubleshooting quick hits

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| MBF cannot see the headset | Use a data-capable USB cable, accept the ADB prompt, install/repair ADB drivers, close SideQuest |
| Browser unsupported | Use current Edge or Chrome |
| "Multiple accounts" error | Remove secondary accounts from the headset |
| Patched but no mods appear | Reopen MBF, verify the patch, install a core mod to test |
| Game crashes after adding a mod | Remove the last mod; check its game version |
| Official multiplayer unavailable | Expected; use Beat Together + MultiplayerCore |

```text
└── <extra files from fileCopies>
```

## `mod.json`

Generated from `mod.template.json`; never edit it by hand.

```json
{
  "_QPVersion": "0.1.1",
  "name": "My Quest Mod",
  "id": "myquestmod",
  "author": "YourName",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "packageId": "com.beatgames.beatsaber",
  "packageVersion": "1.35.0_8016709773",
  "description": "What the mod does.",
  "dependencies": [],
  "modFiles": ["libmyquestmod.so"],
  "libraryFiles": [],
  "coverImage": "cover.png",
  "fileCopies": []
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Stable, unique, matches `qpm.json` `info.id` |
| `version` | SemVer |
| `packageVersion` | Must match the target Beat Saber build |
| `dependencies` | Ids + version ranges of required mods |
| `modFiles` | Leave `${binary}` in the template; QPM resolves it |
| `libraryFiles` | Shared `.so` files your mod needs at runtime |
| `coverImage` | 1024×512, PNG/JPG/GIF, under 2 MB |

## Cover image

1. Create `cover.png` in the project root (1024×512).
2. Add `"coverImage": "cover.png"` to `mod.template.json`.
3. Rebuild the QMOD and verify it appears in MBF/QuestPatcher.

Large or animated covers slow down mod browsing; keep it under 2 MB.

## Extra files

Use `fileCopies` to place data on the device:

```json
"fileCopies": [
  {
    "name": "presets.json",
    "destination": "/sdcard/ModData/com.beatgames.beatsaber/Mods/MyQuestMod/presets.json"
  }
]
```

Add the source file to the package list in `createqmod.ps1` as documented in the template, then rebuild. Use `ModData`, not the game's data folder, for mod-owned files.

## Dependencies and bundling

- Declare runtime mod dependencies in `mod.template.json` `dependencies`.
- Declare build-time QPM dependencies in `qpm.json`.
- Set `"additionalData": { "includeQmod": false }` for loaders/runtime libraries that the user installs separately (for example Scotland2).
- Never bundle another mod's `.so` as `libraryFiles` unless you are certain of the licensing and load behavior.

## Versioning

| Change | Version bump |
| --- | --- |
| Bug fix, no API change | Patch |
| New feature | Minor |
| Config/API break, or new game version only | Major |

Per game version, publish a distinct release and state the supported `packageVersion`. Do not advertise a version range you have not tested.

## Test the package before publishing

1. Uninstall the development copy.
2. Install the `.qmod` through MBF or QuestPatcher.
3. Boot, open every UI page, play a map, change config, restart.
4. Verify the mod appears in the mod list with the right name, version, author, and cover.
5. Check the log for warnings or repeated errors.

`qpm s copy` tests the `.so`, not the package. A mod can work via `copy.ps1` and fail as a QMOD because `mod.json` is wrong.

## Distribution

| Channel | Use |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub Releases | Primary download; attach the `.qmod` and release notes |
| BSQMods (<https://mods.bsquest.xyz>) | Quest mod repository used by MBF; follow its submission instructions |
| BSMG Discord `#quest-mod-dev` / mod channels | Announcements and feedback; not a substitute for a repository listing |

Release notes should include:

- Supported Beat Saber version (`packageVersion`).
- Required dependencies and versions.
- What changed.
- Known incompatibilities.
- Whether saves/config need migration.

## CI and tag-triggered releases

The template ships `.github/workflows/build-ndk.yml`, which builds on Ubuntu with the Android NDK and runs on branches, PRs, and `v*` tags. Adapt it to:

1. Restore QPM dependencies (`Fernthedev/qpm-action@v1` with `restore: true`).
2. Set the NDK path (`ndkpath.txt`) from the setup action.
3. Build the QMOD (`qpm s qmod`).
4. Validate the manifest (`qpm s validate`).
5. Upload the `.qmod` as a workflow artifact.
6. On a `v*` tag, create a GitHub Release for that tag and attach the `.qmod`.

Template: [`../assets/workflows/quest-release.yml.txt`](../assets/workflows/quest-release.yml.txt).

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: true
          lfs: true

      - uses: seanmiddleditch/gha-setup-ninja@v6

      - name: Setup NDK
        id: setup-ndk
        uses: ./.github/actions/canary-ndk

      - name: Create ndkpath.txt
        run: |
          echo ${{ steps.setup-ndk.outputs.ndk-path }} > ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/ndkpath.txt

      - uses: Fernthedev/qpm-action@v1
        with:
          workflow_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          restore: true
          cache: true
          publish: false

      - run: qpm s qmod

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: MyQuestMod-${{ github.ref_name }}
          path: ./MyQuestMod.qmod
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Attach artifacts to the tag
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          name: MyQuestMod ${{ github.ref_name }}
          generate_release_notes: true
          prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          files: |
            ./MyQuestMod.qmod
```

Notes:

- `tag_name: ${{ github.ref_name }}` is explicit. Older template workflows use `github.event.inputs.version`, which is empty on a tag push; omit it or use `github.ref_name`.
- `permissions: contents: write` is required for the release step; organization defaults may be read-only.
- Keep the NDK version in CI identical to local development. A mismatched NDK produces different crash behavior and makes tombstones hard to compare.
- Run `qpm s validate` in CI before packaging so a schema error fails the build instead of shipping a broken QMOD.
- Workflow artifacts expire; release assets do not. Attach the QMOD to the GitHub Release for the tag.

Release procedure:

1. Bump the version in `qpm.json` and `mod.template.json`.
2. Update `packageVersion` if the target game version changed.
3. Commit, push, and confirm the branch build passes.
4. `git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0`.
5. Verify the release page: tag, QMOD asset, and notes.

Pin the NDK version in CI to match local development; a mismatched NDK produces different crash behavior.

## Release checklist

- [ ] Mod ID and name are stable and match across `qpm.json`, `mod.template.json`, and logs.
- [ ] `packageVersion` matches the tested game build.
- [ ] Dependencies declared and version-checked.
- [ ] `qpm s validate` passes.
- [ ] QMOD installs cleanly on a fresh device state.
- [ ] Menu, gameplay, config persistence, and restart tested.
- [ ] Cover image present and under 2 MB.
- [ ] No debug logging every frame.
- [ ] README documents install, requirements, configuration, and known issues.
- [ ] Release notes list the supported game version.

## Uninstall behavior

Users remove the mod through MBF/QuestPatcher. Leave no state that breaks the game if the `.so` disappears:

- Config files under `ModData` can remain.
- Do not patch game files on disk.
- Do not leave scheduled coroutines or persistent GameObjects that assume the mod is present.

# ChroMapper: CMUI, Harmony, and Scenes

Canonical sources: [CMUI](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/tree/master/Assets/__Scripts/CMUI) · [DialogBox.cs](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/Assets/__Scripts/CMUI/DialogBox.cs) · [Harmony docs](https://harmony.pardeike.net/articles/patching.html)

ChroMapper gives plugins a loader and a small UI toolkit. Everything beyond that is done by patching the editor with Harmony and attaching Unity components.

## Harmony

ChroMapper ships `0Harmony.dll` in `ChroMapper_Data\Managed`. Reference that copy; do not add a different Harmony NuGet package.

```csharp
using System.Reflection;
using HarmonyLib;

[Plugin("My Plugin")]
public class Plugin
{
    private const string HarmonyId = "com.example.MyPlugin";
    private Harmony harmony;

    [Init]
    private void Init()
    {
        harmony = new Harmony(HarmonyId);
        harmony.PatchAll(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly());
    }

    [Exit]
    private void Exit()
    {
        harmony.UnpatchSelf();
    }
}
```

- Use a unique reverse-domain ID. Reusing another mod's ID makes `UnpatchSelf()` remove patches you do not own.
- `PatchAll(assembly)` applies every class in the assembly carrying `[HarmonyPatch]`.
- `UnpatchSelf()` removes only that Harmony instance's patches.

### Patch classes

```csharp
using HarmonyLib;

[HarmonyPatch(typeof(PrecisionStepDisplayController), "UpdateText")]
internal static class PrecisionStepDisplayController_UpdateTextPatch
{
    private static bool Prefix(int newSnapping)
    {
        // Return false to replace the original; return true to continue.
        return true;
    }
}
```

| Patch | Runs | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prefix | Before the original | Gate execution (`return false`), validate or replace arguments, capture state |
| Postfix | After the original | Observe completion, read or replace `__result` |
| Transpiler | Compiles into the original IL | Changing internals with no hook point; last resort |
| Finalizer | After the original, including exceptions | Cleanup or exception suppression |

Special parameters: `__instance` (the object), `__result` (return value), `___fieldName` (private field), and the original argument names. A patch must match the target signature; wrong parameter names or types fail at patch time.

### Finding targets

1. Search the ChroMapper source under [`Assets/__Scripts`](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/tree/master/Assets/__Scripts). Read the file for the build you target.
2. Or decompile the installed `Main.dll` with ILSpy or dnSpy. This is the exact assembly the plugin will run against.
3. Use `nameof` when the member is accessible. Use a string for private or internal members:

   ```csharp
   [HarmonyPatch(typeof(SomeEditorClass), nameof(SomeEditorClass.PublicMethod))]
   [HarmonyPatch(typeof(SomeEditorClass), "PrivateMethod")]
   ```

### Rules that prevent most breakage

- Prefer postfix → prefix → transpiler, in that order.
- Patch stable, high-level methods. Avoid constructors, compiler-generated lambdas, and UI internals.
- A patch exception propagates into the caller and can break the editor. Wrap risky code in `try/catch` and log with `Debug.LogException`.
- Patches on per-frame or per-note methods run constantly. Keep them allocation-free where possible.
- A Harmony patch is the most version-sensitive part of a plugin. Pin the ChroMapper build and retest after every update.

## Scenes and Unity components

ChroMapper uses five enabled scenes:

| Build index | Scene | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `00_FirstBoot` | Startup, plugin load, persistent services |
| 1 | `01_SongSelectMenu` | Song selection |
| 2 | `02_SongEditMenu` | Per-song settings and difficulty selection |
| 3 | `03_Mapper` | The actual map editor |
| 4 | `04_Options` | Settings |

Scene indexes come from `ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset`; `99_EditorHelper` and `999_PrefabBuilding` are disabled.

A typical plugin waits for the mapper scene, finds an existing object, and attaches a behaviour:

```csharp
using System.Linq;
using UnityEngine;
using UnityEngine.SceneManagement;

private static void OnSceneLoaded(Scene scene, LoadSceneMode mode)
{
    if (scene.buildIndex != 3) return;

    var target = Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<PrecisionStepDisplayController>()
        .FirstOrDefault(controller => controller.gameObject.scene.IsValid());

    if (target == null) return;
    if (target.gameObject.GetComponent<MyEditorBehaviour>() != null) return;

    target.gameObject.AddComponent<MyEditorBehaviour>();
}
```

- `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<T>()` also returns assets and prefabs. Filter with `gameObject.scene.IsValid()` when you need a live scene object.
- Guard against adding the same component twice when the scene reloads.
- Unsubscribe from `SceneManager.sceneLoaded` in `[Exit]`.
- `MonoBehaviour` gives you `Update`, `StartCoroutine`, and `OnGUI`. Prefer a component over a static update loop.

ChroMapper also has many `public` controller types. If a type is `internal`, publicize `Main` or use reflection; patching a private method by name needs no visibility change.

## CMUI dialogs

CMUI is ChroMapper's component-based UI. Use it instead of building uGUI hierarchies by hand.

```csharp
var dialog = PersistentUI.Instance.CreateNewDialogBox()
    .WithTitle("My Plugin");

dialog.AddComponent<TextComponent>()
    .WithInitialValue("Configure the plugin.");

dialog.AddComponent<ToggleComponent>()
    .WithLabel("Enabled")
    .WithInitialValue(() => Config.Enabled)
    .OnChanged(value => Config.Enabled = value);

dialog.AddComponent<SliderComponent>()
    .WithLabel("Opacity")
    .WithSliderParams(0f, 1f, 0.01f)
    .WithInitialValue(() => Config.Opacity)
    .OnChanged(value => Config.Opacity = value);

dialog.AddFooterButton(() => Config.Save(), "Save");
dialog.Open();
```

### DialogBox

| Member | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `PersistentUI.Instance.CreateNewDialogBox()` | Instantiates the dialog prefab. This is the current name; `PLUGINS.md` still says `CreateDialogBox()` |
| `WithTitle(string)` | Sets a plain title; a localized overload exists |
| `WithNoTitle()` | Removes the title |
| `AddComponent<T>()` | Instantiates a CMUI component from the component store and returns it |
| `AddFooterButton(Action onClick, string label)` | Adds a footer button; clicking it closes the dialog after running the callback |
| `OnQuickSubmit(Action)` | Runs on the quick-submit input |
| `Open()` / `Close()` | Shows or hides the dialog |
| `Clear()` | Removes components |
| `DontDestroyOnClose()` | Keeps the dialog after close. You become responsible for destroying it |

A custom dialog self-destructs when closed **unless** you call `DontDestroyOnClose()`. Do not cache a dialog across closes without that call.

### Components

| Component | Value type | Extra API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TextComponent` | `string` | `WithInitialValue(string)` or localized overload |
| `TextBoxComponent` | `string` | `OnEndEdit`, `OnSelect`, `OnDeselect`, `WithContentType`, `WithLineType`, `WithMaximumLength` |
| `ToggleComponent` | `bool` | `WithInitialValue`, `OnChanged` |
| `SliderComponent` | `float` | `WithSliderParams(min, max, precision)`, `WithDisplay`, `WithCustomDisplayFormatter` |
| `DropdownComponent` | `int` | `WithOptions<T>(IEnumerable<T>)`, `WithOptions<T>()` for enums |
| `ButtonComponent` | — | `OnClick`, `WithLabel`, `WithBackgroundColor` |
| `ColorPickerComponent` | colour | Adds a colour picker |
| `NestedColorPickerComponent` | colour | Nested picker |
| `ProgressBarComponent` | — | Progress display |

Common chaining methods:

```csharp
component.WithLabel("Label");          // plain text
component.WithLabel(table, key);       // localized
component.WithNoLabel();
component.WithInitialValue(value);     // value overload
component.WithInitialValue(() => value); // accessor overload
component.OnChanged(value => { });
```

`TextComponent` extends `CMUIComponent<string>` rather than `CMUIComponentWithLabel<string>`, so `WithLabel` does not apply to it. `ButtonComponent` extends `CMUIComponentBase`, so it has no value or `OnChanged`.

### CMUI outside a dialog

`DialogBox.AddComponent<T>()` is the supported path for plugin dialogs. To attach a component to your own UI, use the component store:

```csharp
var component = ComponentStoreSO.Instance.InstantiateCMUIComponentForComponentType(typeof(ToggleComponent));
var handled = ComponentStoreSO.Instance.InstantiateCMUIComponentForHandledType(typeof(bool));
```

You own the lifetime of components created this way; cache and destroy them yourself.

### UI rules

- Create components through the store or `AddComponent<T>()`; do not `new` a MonoBehaviour.
- Do not block the main thread. Use a coroutine for multi-frame work.
- Keep the dialog small and put advanced options behind a second dialog.
- Persist settings yourself; CMUI is presentation only. Write JSON to `Application.persistentDataPath`, not into the read-only install directory.

## Configuration

ChroMapper has no plugin config system. Common approaches:

- `JsonUtility` with a `[Serializable]` class, written to `Application.persistentDataPath`.
- `Plugins.dll` (SimpleJSON) or your own serializer.
- A static `Config` class with a `Save()` method called from a footer button or `OnChanged`.

Do not assume the ChroMapper install directory is writable. Users may install under a protected path, and the launcher may replace the folder on update.

# ChroMapper: Distribution and Support

Canonical pages: [PLUGINS.md legal section](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/PLUGINS.md) · [ChroMapper license (GPLv2)](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/LICENSE) · [ChroMapper Discord](https://discord.gg/YmEt9EZ8pw)

## Package

Ship the plugin as a zip or as a single DLL. The install step must be obvious: extract into `Plugins` and restart ChroMapper.

Recommended layout:

```text
MyPlugin-v1.2.0-cm0.13.892.zip
├── MyPlugin.dll
├── MyPlugin.pdb              (optional, for readable stack traces)
├── dependencies\             (only DLLs ChroMapper does not already ship)
│   └── SomeLibrary.dll
├── README.md
└── LICENSE
```

Rules:

- **Do not include** `Main.dll`, `Plugins.dll`, `0Harmony.dll`, `Input.dll`, `LiteNetLib.dll`, `FileBrowser.dll`, `Intersections.dll`, or any `UnityEngine.*` / `Unity.*` assembly. ChroMapper already has them, and duplicates break the host.
- Include only third-party dependencies that are not part of ChroMapper. Check their licenses.
- Put the tested ChroMapper version in the zip name and the release title. Example: `MyPlugin-v1.2.0-cm0.13.892.zip`.
- If the plugin has a folder with dependencies, tell users to copy the **whole folder** into `Plugins`.

## README checklist

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Requirements | ChroMapper build tested, OS support, any other plugin needed |
| Install | Exact folder, zip contents, restart step |
| Uninstall | Delete the DLL/folder |
| Features | What it adds, with screenshots or a short clip |
| Known issues | Version-specific breakage, conflicts |
| Source and license | Repository URL and license |
| Support | Where to report bugs and what to attach |

State the tested build explicitly. "Works with ChroMapper" is not enough; a plugin is bound to a build.

## Release checklist

1. Rebuild against the exact ChroMapper build you tested.
2. Bump `AssemblyVersion`; the Options → Plugins list displays it.
3. Test on a clean ChroMapper install with only this plugin.
4. Test the install steps from the zip, not from your development output folder.
5. Tag the release with the same version used by the optional update manifest.
6. Attach the zip to a GitHub Release and write the tested ChroMapper version in the title.
7. Announce in the ChroMapper Discord `#plugins` channel if appropriate.

There is no official repository to submit to. ChroMapper's wiki plugin page lists only a couple of plugins; the Discord `#plugins` channel and GitHub are the practical distribution channels.

## Optional: ChroMapper-UpdateChecker manifest

[ChroMapper-UpdateChecker](https://github.com/LightAi39/ChroMapper-UpdateChecker) scans plugins for an embedded `manifest.json` and compares the `version` field with the latest GitHub release tag. It is a community plugin, not a ChroMapper standard.

Embed [manifest.json.txt](../assets/manifest.json.txt) as an **embedded resource**:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <EmbeddedResource Include="manifest.json" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Format — every field is required:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Stable identifier |
| `name` | Display name |
| `author` | Author name |
| `version` | Must exactly match the GitHub release tag, including a leading `v` if you use one |
| `description` | One line |
| `git` | Repository main page URL |

The checker compares `version` to the tag on the release GitHub marks as **latest**. If they do not match, users see `name - [local version] > [latest version]`. Bump the manifest in the same commit as the version bump, and publish the matching release tag.

## Versioning

- ChroMapper has no plugin API version. Your version communicates compatibility, so include the ChroMapper build in the release metadata.
- A single plugin version should target one ChroMapper build. If you support two builds, publish two releases or two DLLs.
- Semver is fine for the plugin itself, but it says nothing about ChroMapper compatibility.
- Do not claim support for dev-channel builds unless you tested them.

## Licensing

ChroMapper is licensed under **GPLv2**. The plugin guide contains the project author's position:

> If identifiable sections of that work are not derived from the Program, and can be reasonably considered independent and separate works in themselves, then this License, and its terms, do not apply to those sections when you distribute them as separate works.

The author states that plugins distributed separately are treated as independent works, so GPLv2's source-distribution requirements are not applied to them. That is the ChroMapper project's interpretation, **not legal advice**.

Practical consequences:

- A plugin that only references `Main.dll` and uses public APIs is treated as a separate work by the project.
- If you copy ChroMapper source code, assets, or substantial internal logic into your plugin, it is a derivative work and GPLv2 applies. Do not copy source unless you are prepared to license the result under GPLv2.
- Do not redistribute ChroMapper, Unity, or Beat Saber binaries. Point users at the official launcher.
- Check the license of every bundled third-party library.
- Include a `LICENSE` file in the release.

## Security expectations

- Publish source, or at least a reproducible build, so users can inspect what runs on their machine.
- Do not download and execute code at runtime without explicit user action. If the plugin has an updater, show what will be downloaded.
- Do not request elevation. ChroMapper does not need Administrator rights, and a plugin that asks for them is suspicious.
- Do not bundle telemetry without disclosure.
- Avoid obfuscation; it makes the plugin indistinguishable from malware to users.

## Support triage

Ask for these before guessing:

1. **ChroMapper version.** It is displayed in the Options screen.
2. **Plugin name and version.** Options → Plugins shows `Name` and `v<assembly version>`.
3. **Install path.** Confirm `<folder with ChroMapper.exe>\Plugins` and that the path is writable and plain ASCII.
4. **Other plugins.** Ask the user to move all other plugins out and retest. The loader is not failure-isolated, so one bad DLL can hide the rest.
5. **Log.** Request `ChroMapper.log` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\BinaryElement\ChroMapper\ChroMapper.log`) or the full console output.
6. **Reproduction steps and the exact error text.** A screenshot of a stack trace is not enough; the log has the full trace.

Triage order:

```text
version mismatch -> install path/permissions -> isolation test -> log/stack trace -> reproduce -> fix or document
```

If the plugin is listed but does nothing, suspect a version mismatch or a Harmony target change before suspecting the user's install.

## CI note

ChroMapper assemblies are not published on NuGet, and redistributing them from your repository is not appropriate. A CI build therefore needs a ChroMapper install available on the runner:

- Cache an official ChroMapper install obtained through the launcher or Jenkins, then set `ChroMapperDir`.
- Build with MSBuild and publish the zip on a tag.
- If you cannot provision ChroMapper in CI, document a manual release build rather than shipping an unverified artifact.

Do not make CI depend on a random third-party mirror. Use the official launcher or the project's Jenkins build.
