# ChroMapper: Install and Troubleshoot Plugins

Canonical pages: [Plugin guide](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/PLUGINS.md) · [Settings - Plugins](https://chromapper.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UG/pages/2916361/Settings+-+Plugins) · [FAQ](https://chromapper.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UG/pages/806682666)

## What a plugin is

ChroMapper's only extension mechanism is the plugin: a managed `.dll` placed under `Plugins`. The editor's own loader scans that folder at startup, constructs every exported type carrying `[Plugin]`, and calls its `[Init]` method. ChroMapper does not provide a separate "mod" format, a downloader, or a dependency manager.

## Where the folder is

The folder is `Plugins` **relative to the ChroMapper executable**:

```text
<ChroMapper install>\
├── ChroMapper.exe
├── ChroMapper_Data\
│   └── Managed\          <- Main.dll and Unity assemblies live here
└── Plugins\              <- plugins go here
```

The recommended install path is the ChroMapper Launcher (CML): <https://cm.topc.at/dl>. CML downloads and patches ChroMapper into a `chromapper` folder next to `CML.exe`. A common layout is:

```text
C:\TOOL\ChroMapper\
├── CML.exe
└── chromapper\
    ├── ChroMapper.exe
    ├── ChroMapper_Data\
    └── Plugins\
```

If `Plugins` does not exist, **Options → Plugins → Open Plugins Folder** creates it and opens it in the file browser. The loader also creates it on startup if it is missing.

Use a plain-ASCII, user-writable path. The wiki FAQ calls out restricted locations such as the Windows `Downloads` folder as the usual cause of plugins not loading; the Japanese setup guide recommends a folder such as `C:\TOOL\ChroMapper` with only half-width alphanumerics.

## Install, update, remove

1. Close ChroMapper. A running instance locks plugin DLLs.
2. Extract the release into `Plugins`. Either drop the single DLL there or copy the whole plugin folder, including any bundled dependencies. The loader searches `Plugins` recursively.
3. Start ChroMapper.
4. Open **Options → Plugins**. Each loaded plugin is listed with its display name and `v<assembly version>`; the header shows `Loaded Plugins: <count>`. The tab hides itself when the count is zero.
5. To update, replace the old DLL or folder while ChroMapper is closed. To remove, delete the DLL or folder. There is no enable/disable, no uninstaller, and no plugin settings page in ChroMapper itself.

Uninstalling ChroMapper is done by deleting the `chromapper` folder next to the launcher, then letting CML reinstall. Plugins live inside that folder and are removed with it.

## Where plugins come from

There is **no official plugin repository**. Distribution is community-driven:

| Channel | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| ChroMapper Discord, `#plugins` | The FAQ points here for the recommended error checker, CM-JS. Invite: <https://discord.gg/YmEt9EZ8pw> |
| GitHub Releases | Most plugins publish a DLL or zip and state the ChroMapper build they were tested on |
| Wiki plugin list | Lists [CM-ErrorChecker](https://github.com/Top-Cat/CM-ErrorChecker/releases/latest) and [CM-OSC](https://github.com/Top-Cat/CM-OSC/releases/latest) |

Notable community plugins, useful when a user describes a feature rather than a name:

| Plugin | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| CM-JS / CM-ErrorChecker | Error checking plus user JavaScript checks; the editor's de facto replacement for MMA2's error checker. The original is [Top-Cat/CM-ErrorChecker](https://github.com/Top-Cat/CM-ErrorChecker); a newer community fork is [XAce1337manX/CM-ErrorChecker](https://github.com/XAce1337manX/CM-ErrorChecker) |
| ChroMapper-AutoModder | Auto-checking, comments, and review workflow aimed at BeatLeader ranking |
| CM-OSC | Sends ChroMapper state over OSC |
| ChroMapper-UpdateChecker | Flags outdated plugins by reading an embedded `manifest.json` |

Do not assume a Beat Saber mod repository carries ChroMapper plugins. The BeatMods ecosystem targets Beat Saber; ChroMapper plugins are published by their authors.

## Version compatibility

ChroMapper has **no plugin API version and no compatibility check**. The loader loads any DLL it finds, then fails later if types or methods no longer exist. Consequences:

- Pin releases to a ChroMapper build, and say so in the release title and README. `ChroMapper-AutoModder` does this explicitly, for example "for ChroMapper v0.13.892 (Stable Release Channel)".
- A plugin built for a stable build may work on a nearby dev build, but it is not guaranteed. Treat dev builds as unsupported until tested.
- When ChroMapper updates and a plugin breaks, the fix is a rebuilt plugin, not a config change.
- The loader displays `AssemblyName.Version`, so a plugin's version in the UI is its assembly version, not the GitHub tag.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Checks and fixes |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin never appears in Options → Plugins | Confirm the path is `<folder containing ChroMapper.exe>\Plugins`, not `ChroMapper_Data\Plugins`. Confirm the file ends in `.dll`. Confirm the DLL is readable and not quarantined by antivirus. |
| Plugin appears only sometimes | Close ChroMapper before copying; a locked DLL silently stays old. Re-copy and restart. |
| "Incompatible plugin X, please check for an update or remove it!" | The loader constructed the type and it threw, or the constructor failed. Usual causes: the class is not public, has no public parameterless constructor, has two methods with the same loader attribute, or has a missing dependency. Update or remove it. |
| Plugin loads but its feature is missing | Built for another ChroMapper version, a Harmony target moved, or a bundled dependency is missing. Check the log for the first exception, then rebuild. |
| Every plugin stopped loading after adding one | The scan is not failure-isolated: `Assembly.LoadFile` and `GetExportedTypes()` run outside the per-type try/catch. One bad DLL can abort the rest of the scan. Move DLLs out in halves until loading returns. |
| ChroMapper will not start after installing a plugin | Remove the newest plugin and retry. Then bisect. |
| Plugin works on Windows but not on macOS/Linux | Plugins are .NET Framework assemblies; support depends on the plugin and the platform build. Do not promise parity. |

Installing into `Program Files` can require elevation. Prefer a user-writable folder; a plugin that asks for Administrator rights is suspicious.

## Logs and console

- ChroMapper writes `ChroMapper.log` under Unity's persistent data path. On Windows:

  ```text
  %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\BinaryElement\ChroMapper\ChroMapper.log
  ```

- The in-game developer console auto-opens for errors, exceptions, and non-important errors when enabled. It also inspects stack traces and prints:

  ```text
  The following exception is caused by the '<plugin>' plugin, please check for an update or remove it!
  ```

  This is the fastest way to attribute a crash to a plugin.
- `Debug.Log`, `Debug.LogWarning`, and `Debug.LogException` from a plugin all land in the same log. Ask users for the whole file, not a screenshot of one line.
- A plugin's `[Init]` failure logs `Error Loading Plugin: <name> - v<version>` and still leaves the plugin in the loaded list. The UI listing alone does not prove the plugin initialised successfully.

## Security model

ChroMapper loads plugins in-process with full user rights. There is no signature verification, no sandbox, no permission prompt, and no virus scanning. The in-game Plugins tab carries this warning:

> ChroMapper developers will not be held liable for any damage caused by loaded plugins. It is up to the user to decide which plugins they want to install. We recommend finding plugins made by trustworthy developers. For example, look for ChroMapper plugins that are open source, where its internal source code is available for all to look through and make their own informed decisions.

Practical rules:

- Prefer open-source plugins with a public build.
- Download from the author's GitHub release or the Discord `#plugins` channel, not from reupload sites.
- Delete the plugin if the source is unavailable and the author is unknown.
- A plugin can read and write maps, settings, and any file the user can access. Treat it with the same trust as any desktop application.

## macOS and Linux

CML ships builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and ChroMapper itself is cross-platform. The plugin format is the same: a managed DLL under `Plugins` next to the executable. Paths and permissions differ:

- Use a path the user owns; avoid system directories.
- The same version-matching and failure-isolation rules apply.
- The log path follows Unity's persistent data path for the platform; the in-game console is the reliable fallback.

# ChroMapper: Plugin API

Canonical sources: [PLUGINS.md](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/PLUGINS.md) · [`Assets/__Scripts/PluginLoader`](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/tree/master/Assets/__Scripts/PluginLoader) · [`Assets/__Scripts/Requirements`](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/tree/master/Assets/__Scripts/Requirements)

ChroMapper's plugin API is deliberately small. The loader discovers types, calls lifecycle methods, and exposes a few registration hooks. Everything else is done with Harmony patches and Unity APIs.

## How the loader works

Simplified from `PluginLoader.LoadAssemblies()`:

```csharp
foreach (var file in Directory.GetFiles("Plugins", "*.dll", SearchOption.AllDirectories))
{
    var assembly = Assembly.LoadFile(Path.GetFullPath(file));

    foreach (var type in assembly.GetExportedTypes())
    {
        var pluginAttribute = type.GetCustomAttribute<PluginAttribute>();
        if (pluginAttribute == null) continue;

        var plugin = new Plugin(pluginAttribute.Name, assembly.GetName(),
            Activator.CreateInstance(type));
        plugins.Add(plugin);
    }
}

foreach (var plugin in plugins)
    plugin.Init();

PluginsLoadedEvent.Invoke(plugins.ToArray());
```

What this means in practice:

- The scan is recursive under `Plugins`, so a plugin folder can hold its own dependency DLLs.
- `Assembly.LoadFile` is used; there is no load-context isolation, dependency resolver, or per-plugin unload.
- Only **public exported types** are considered.
- The type must have a **public parameterless constructor**.
- Every plugin is constructed before any `[Init]` runs. There is no dependency order.
- File enumeration order is not guaranteed.
- `Assembly.LoadFile` and `GetExportedTypes()` are **not** wrapped in the per-type try/catch. A missing dependency or unreadable assembly can abort the rest of the scan. Failure isolation is the user's job: remove plugins until loading returns.

## The plugin class

```csharp
[Plugin("My ChroMapper Plugin")]
public class Plugin
{
    [Init]
    private void Init() { }

    [Exit]
    private void Exit() { }
}
```

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Attribute | `[Plugin("Display Name")]` — the string is display-only |
| Visibility | `public`; nested or internal types are skipped |
| Constructor | Public parameterless constructor; the loader calls `Activator.CreateInstance` |
| Methods | Instance or static, public or private. Binding flags include `NonPublic` |
| Attribute count | Exactly one method per attribute type. A duplicate makes the `Plugin` constructor throw and the loader report "Incompatible plugin" |
| Namespace | Any. Give the class a namespace so it does not collide with ChroMapper's own `Plugin` type |

`Plugin` objects expose:

| Member | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | The `[Plugin]` display name |
| `Version` | `AssemblyName.Version` — set with `[assembly: AssemblyVersion(...)]` |
| `AssemblyName` | Full assembly identity |

The Options → Plugins list renders `Name` and `v{Version}`. `AssemblyVersion("1.2.3.0")` displays as `v1.2.3.0`; there is no trimming.

## Lifecycle and callbacks

| Attribute | Fires | Argument | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[Init]` | Once, after every plugin is constructed | none | Main setup: Harmony, event subscriptions, UI registration |
| `[ObjectLoaded]` | When a map object's container is spawned in the editor | `Beatmap.Containers.ObjectContainer` | Fired by `BeatmapObjectContainerCollection` on container spawn |
| `[EventPassedThreshold]` | When playback passes a light event | `Beatmap.Base.BaseObject` | Fired by `PluginEventHandler`; high frequency |
| `[NotePassedThreshold]` | When playback passes a note | `Beatmap.Base.BaseObject` | Fired by `PluginEventHandler`; high frequency |
| `[Exit]` | When the plugin loader is destroyed (normally application quit) | none | Unpatch Harmony, unsubscribe events, stop coroutines |

Rules:

- The argument type must match. A wrong parameter type fails at invoke time.
- `[Init]` exceptions are caught, logged with the inner exception, and reported as `Error Loading Plugin: <name> - v<version>`. The plugin still remains in the loaded list, so a UI listing does not prove successful initialisation.
- Keep `[Init]` fast. The loader runs it synchronously during startup.
- Do not assume another plugin has initialised before yours. If you need cross-plugin coordination, use `PluginsLoadedEvent` (see below) or defer work until a scene loads.

## Loader access from a plugin

`PluginLoader` is `internal`, so a normal plugin cannot reference `PluginLoader.LoadedPlugins` or `PluginsLoadedEvent`. The members are:

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<Plugin> LoadedPlugins { get; }
public static Action<Plugin[]> PluginsLoadedEvent;
```

Options:

- Add Krafs.Publicizer and `<Publicize Include="Main" />` (see [project-setup.md](project-setup.md)).
- Use reflection against `PluginLoader` in `Main.dll`.

There is no plugin dependency declaration, no service registry, and no load-order control. If two plugins must cooperate, discover each other through public types or a shared file, and make the integration optional.

## Requirement checks

`RequirementCheck` lets a plugin add its own mod or feature to a map's `_requirements` or `_suggestions`. The abstract API in the **current source** is:

```csharp
using Beatmap.Base;
using Beatmap.Info;

public class MyModCheck : RequirementCheck
{
    public override string Name => "MyMod";

    public override RequirementType IsRequiredOrSuggested(
        InfoDifficulty infoDifficulty, BaseDifficulty map)
    {
        if (/* map uses MyMod data */ false)
            return RequirementType.Requirement;

        return RequirementType.None;
    }
}
```

Register it before the editor needs it:

```csharp
[Plugin("My Plugin")]
public class Plugin
{
    [Init]
    private void Init() =>
        RequirementCheck.RegisterRequirement(new MyModCheck());
}
```

| Member | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `Name` | Written verbatim into `_requirements` / `_suggestions`; match the name the game mod declares |
| `IsRequiredOrSuggested` | Return `Requirement`, `Suggestion`, or `None` |
| `RegisterRequirement` | Adds the instance to a static `HashSet<RequirementCheck>`; keep one stable instance instead of registering repeatedly |

Caveats:

- The signature in `PLUGINS.md` is stale: it shows `BeatSaberSong.DifficultyBeatmap mapInfo, BeatSaberMap map`. Current code uses `InfoDifficulty` and `BaseDifficulty`. Compile against the build you target.
- Built-in checks (Chroma 2.0, Chroma 1.0, Noodle Extensions, Mapping Extensions, Cinema, Sound Extensions, Vivify) are registered by `RequirementCheck.Setup()` when `PersistentUI` starts. `Setup()` clears the static set first, so a registration made before it runs is lost. The documented place is `[Init]`; if the check does not survive, register again after startup with a Harmony postfix on `RequirementCheck.Setup()` or a one-shot scene-loaded hook.
- A check runs whenever ChroMapper evaluates requirements. Keep it cheap and side-effect free.

## Extension buttons

`ExtensionButtons` registers buttons in the mapper's right-side pop-out panel.

```csharp
using UnityEngine;

[Plugin("My Plugin")]
public class Plugin
{
    [Init]
    private void Init()
    {
        ExtensionButton button = ExtensionButtons.AddButton(
            iconSprite, "My tooltip", OnButtonClick);

        button.Visible = true;
        button.Interactable = true;
    }

    private void OnButtonClick() { }
}
```

| Member | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| `ExtensionButtons.AddButton(Sprite icon, string tooltip, UnityAction onClick)` | Creates and registers a button |
| `ExtensionButtons.AddButton(ExtensionButton button)` | Registers a preconfigured button |
| `ExtensionButtons.RemoveButton(ExtensionButton button)` | Unregisters it |
| `ExtensionButton.Tooltip` | Hover text |
| `ExtensionButton.Icon` | `Sprite` shown on the button |
| `ExtensionButton.Click` | `UnityAction` invoked on click |
| `ExtensionButton.Visible` / `Interactable` | Show/hide and enable/disable |

Register in `[Init]`, or at least before the mapper scene loads. The button object is a plain C# object; keep a reference if you need to change its state later.

## Versioning and API stability

- ChroMapper is GPLv2 and developed in the open; the source is the specification.
- There is no semantic version for the plugin API. A minor editor release can rename a private method that a Harmony patch targets.
- `master` can be ahead of the stable build. Read the source at the tag matching the installed build when you need exact signatures.
- Pin a tested ChroMapper version in the README and release notes.
- Prefer public APIs and Harmony patches on stable, high-level methods. Avoid patching compiler-generated closures, UI internals, and constructors.

# ChroMapper: Plugin Project Setup

Canonical pages: [PLUGINS.md](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/PLUGINS.md) · [BUILD.md](https://github.com/Caeden117/ChroMapper/blob/master/BUILD.md)

## What you are building

A ChroMapper plugin is a **.NET Framework 4.8 class library** that references the assemblies shipped with ChroMapper and copies its output into `Plugins`. It is not a Unity project, not a BepInEx plugin, and not a Beat Saber mod.

ChroMapper 0.13.892 uses Unity **2021.3.45f1**. Its build guide recommends the Mono backend; IL2CPP breaks Harmony-dependent features. Match the build you target: a plugin compiled against a different ChroMapper build may load and then fail at runtime.

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| ChroMapper | A real install, launched at least once. Get it through [CML](https://cm.topc.at/dl) |
| IDE | Visual Studio 2022 (recommended) or Rider. The official guide uses Visual Studio |
| .NET Framework 4.8 targeting pack | Required to compile `net48`; install it as an individual component in the VS installer |
| Harmony | Bundled with ChroMapper as `0Harmony.dll`; do not add your own Harmony package |

The official workflow is Windows-centric. macOS and Linux can compile with Mono/MSBuild, but the templates and community tooling assume Windows. Say so rather than promising a cross-platform build.

## 1. Point the project at ChroMapper

Set a `ChroMapperDir` environment variable to the folder that contains `ChroMapper.exe`:

```text
ChroMapperDir = C:\TOOL\ChroMapper\chromapper
```

Verify that this file exists before opening the IDE:

```text
%ChroMapperDir%\ChroMapper_Data\Managed\Main.dll
```

MSBuild imports environment variables as properties, so `$(ChroMapperDir)` works in the project file without any extra props file. A `Directory.Build.props` next to the solution also works:

```xml
<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <ChroMapperDir>C:\TOOL\ChroMapper\chromapper</ChroMapperDir>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

Do not commit a machine-specific `ChroMapperDir`. Keep it in the environment or in an untracked local props file.

## 2. Create the project

1. Create a **Class Library (.NET Framework)** targeting **.NET Framework 4.8**.
2. Name the assembly after the plugin, for example `MyChroMapperPlugin`. The assembly name is not the display name.
3. Replace the generated project file with [ChroMapperPlugin.csproj.txt](../assets/ChroMapperPlugin.csproj.txt), or edit the references by hand using the table below. The asset also expects `Plugin.cs` and `HarmonyPatch.cs`; copy both or remove the `HarmonyPatch.cs` compile item.
4. Add an `[assembly: AssemblyVersion("1.0.0.0")]` attribute. The Options → Plugins list displays this value.

If you prefer the community starting points instead of the asset:

| Template | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| [Vainstains/ChroMapperPluginTemplate](https://github.com/Vainstains/ChroMapperPluginTemplate) | `dotnet new` template; assumes `ChroMapperDir`; already wires Krafs.Publicizer and a post-build copy |
| [rynan4818/ChroMapperPluginTemplates](https://github.com/rynan4818/ChroMapperPluginTemplates) | Visual Studio 2022 project template; Japanese wiki contains a translation of the official plugin guide |
| [rynan4818/ChroMapper-PrecisionStepAdditions](https://github.com/rynan4818/ChroMapper-PrecisionStepAdditions) | Full working plugin: Harmony patches, scene hook, configuration, and custom UI |

## 3. References

All paths are under `%ChroMapperDir%\ChroMapper_Data\Managed\`.

| Assembly | When you need it |
| --- | --- |
| `Main.dll` | Always. Plugin attributes, loader types, editor classes, CMUI, `PersistentUI`, `RequirementCheck`, `ExtensionButtons` |
| `Plugins.dll` | ChroMapper's SimpleJSON library, if you do not want to add your own JSON dependency |
| `0Harmony.dll` | Harmony patches. Use the bundled copy so patch state matches the host |
| `UnityEngine.CoreModule.dll` | `GameObject`, `Debug`, `Resources`, `Sprite`, `Application`, coroutines |
| `UnityEngine.UI.dll` | uGUI controls |
| `UnityEngine.UIModule.dll` | Canvas and UI infrastructure |
| `UnityEngine.InputLegacyModule.dll` | Legacy `Input` API |
| `Unity.InputSystem.dll` | The Input System used by ChroMapper |
| `Unity.TextMeshPro.dll` | TextMeshPro text |
| `UnityEngine.ImageConversionModule.dll` | `Texture2D.EncodeToPNG` and image conversion |
| `UnityEngine.AudioModule.dll` | Audio playback |
| `UnityEngine.TextRenderingModule.dll` | Fonts and text rendering |
| `UnityEngine.UnityWebRequestModule.dll` | HTTP requests |
| `FileBrowser.dll` | ChroMapper's cross-platform file browser |
| `Intersections.dll` | ChroMapper's raycasting system |
| `Input.dll` | ChroMapper's input actions |
| `LiteNetLib.dll` | Networking, only if the plugin needs it |

Two rules for every ChroMapper and Unity reference:

```xml
<Reference Include="Main">
  <HintPath>$(ChroMapperDir)\ChroMapper_Data\Managed\Main.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>False</Private>
</Reference>
```

- **`<Private>False</Private>` (Copy Local = false).** Never copy `Main.dll`, `0Harmony.dll`, or Unity assemblies into `Plugins`. The host already has them; duplicates cause type-identity mismatches and can break Harmony.
- **Reference the installed assemblies, not NuGet packages.** There is no ChroMapper NuGet package and no supported substitute.

`System`, `System.Core`, `System.Data`, and `System.Xml` are ordinary framework references and can stay.

## 4. Publicizer only when you need internals

Most plugin-facing APIs are public: `Plugin`/`[Plugin]`, `[Init]`, `[Exit]`, `ExtensionButtons`, `RequirementCheck`, `PersistentUI`, `DialogBox`, and the CMUI components.

`PluginLoader` is **internal**, so `PluginLoader.LoadedPlugins` and `PluginLoader.PluginsLoadedEvent` are not visible to a normal plugin. To reach them, add [Krafs.Publicizer](https://github.com/Krafs/Publicizer):

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <PackageReference Include="Krafs.Publicizer" Version="2.3.0" PrivateAssets="all" />
</ItemGroup>

<ItemGroup>
  <!-- Publicize only the assembly you need. -->
  <Publicize Include="Main" />
</ItemGroup>
```

Publicizer defaults to publicizing **nothing**. `<PublicizeAll>true</PublicizeAll>` publicizes every referenced assembly, which is usually broader than necessary. The alternative to publicizing is reflection:

```csharp
var loaderType = Type.GetType("PluginLoader, Main");
var loaded = loaderType?.GetProperty("LoadedPlugins", BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static)
    ?.GetValue(null);
```

Prefer public APIs; internals change without notice.

## 5. Build and deploy

The project asset runs a post-build copy:

```xml
<Target Name="Deploy" AfterTargets="Build" Condition="'$(ChroMapperDir)' != ''">
  <MakeDir Directories="$(ChroMapperDir)\Plugins" />
  <Copy SourceFiles="$(TargetPath)" DestinationFolder="$(ChroMapperDir)\Plugins" />
  <Copy SourceFiles="$(TargetDir)$(TargetName).pdb"
        DestinationFolder="$(ChroMapperDir)\Plugins"
        Condition="Exists('$(TargetDir)$(TargetName).pdb')" />
</Target>
```

If the copy fails with a sharing violation, ChroMapper is still running and holds the DLL open. Close it and rebuild.

For a release, copy only the plugin DLL and any dependency DLLs that are **not** shipped with ChroMapper. Ship the PDB only if you want readable stack traces; it is not required.

## 6. Test

1. Launch ChroMapper from the same install that `ChroMapperDir` points at.
2. Open **Options → Plugins**. The plugin must appear with its display name and assembly version.
3. Exercise the feature in the editor.
4. Read `ChroMapper.log` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\BinaryElement\ChroMapper\ChroMapper.log`) and the in-game console.

Plugins are **not loaded in the Unity Editor**. `PluginLoader` contains `private const bool loadPluginsInEditor = false;`. Testing inside Unity requires building ChroMapper from source and changing that constant, which is a development-only change. The normal loop is: build the DLL, copy it into `Plugins`, launch the player, read the log.

For breakpoints, the practical options are:

- Log-driven debugging (`Debug.Log`, `Debug.LogException`) against the shipped player.
- Build ChroMapper from source in Unity 2021.3.45f1 and attach to the player/editor. BUILD.md explicitly recommends the Mono backend; IL2CPP breaks Harmony-dependent features.

Do not tell users to replace their ChroMapper install with a debug build to troubleshoot a plugin.

## 7. Common build and load errors

| Error | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MSB3245` or unresolved `Main.dll` | `ChroMapperDir` unset or pointing at the wrong folder | Set it to the folder containing `ChroMapper.exe`; confirm `ChroMapper_Data\Managed\Main.dll` exists |
| `CS0246` type or namespace not found | Missing reference for the Unity module or ChroMapper assembly | Add the assembly from `ChroMapper_Data\Managed` |
| `CS0122` inaccessible due to protection level | You are using an `internal` ChroMapper type | Publicize `Main` or use reflection |
| Post-build copy fails | ChroMapper is running and locks the DLL | Close ChroMapper, rebuild |
| Plugin appears but logs "Incompatible plugin" | Class not public, no public parameterless constructor, or two methods share one loader attribute | Fix the type; one method per `[Init]`/`[Exit]`/event attribute |
| `FileNotFoundException` for a dependency | Bundled dependency missing from the plugin folder | Copy the dependency DLL next to the plugin |
| Plugin works in one ChroMapper build and not another | Version mismatch | Rebuild against the running build |

## 8. Language level

Unity 2021.3 supports C# 9. Set `<LangVersion>9.0</LangVersion>` unless you have a reason to go higher. Records and `init` accessors need an `IsExternalInit` shim on `net48`; avoid them for a plugin that has to stay simple.

## Entropy-Based Detection

Apply to string literals > 20 characters in assignment context.
High entropy (Shannon entropy > 4.5 bits/char) + length > 20 = likely secret.

```
Calculate entropy: -sum(p * log2(p)) for each character frequency p
Threshold: > 4.5 bits/char AND > 20 chars AND assigned to a variable
```

Common false positives to exclude:
- Lorem ipsum text
- HTML/CSS content
- Base64-encoded non-sensitive config (but flag and note)
- UUID/GUID (entropy is high but format is recognizable)

## 1. Injection Flaws

### SQL Injection
**What to look for:**
- String concatenation or interpolation inside SQL queries
- Raw `.query()`, `.execute()`, `.raw()` calls with variables
- ORM `whereRaw()`, `selectRaw()`, `orderByRaw()` with user input
- Second-order SQLi: data stored safely, then used unsafely later
- Stored procedures called with unsanitized input

**Detection signals (all languages):**
```
"SELECT ... " + variable
`SELECT ... ${variable}`
f"SELECT ... {variable}"
"SELECT ... %s" % variable   # Only safe with proper driver parameterization
cursor.execute("... " + input)
db.raw(`... ${req.params.id}`)
```

**Safe patterns (parameterized):**
```js
db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', [userId])
User.findOne({ where: { id: userId } })  // ORM safe
```

**Escalation checkers:**
- Is the query result ever used in another query? (second-order)
- Is the table/column name user-controlled? (cannot be parameterized — must allowlist)

---

### Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
**What to look for:**
- `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `document.write()` with user data
- `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in React
- Template engines rendering unescaped: `{{{ var }}}` (Handlebars), `!= var` (Pug)
- jQuery `.html()`, `.append()` with user data
- `eval()`, `setTimeout(string)`, `setInterval(string)` with user data
- DOM-based: `location.hash`, `document.referrer`, `window.name` written to DOM
- Stored XSS: user input saved to DB, rendered without escaping later

**Detection by framework:**
- **React**: Safe by default EXCEPT `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
- **Angular**: Safe by default EXCEPT `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`
- **Vue**: Safe by default EXCEPT `v-html`
- **Vanilla JS**: Every DOM write is suspect

---

### Command Injection
**What to look for (Node.js):**
```js
exec(userInput)
execSync(`ping ${host}`)
spawn('sh', ['-c', userInput])
child_process.exec('ls ' + dir)
```

**What to look for (Python):**
```python
os.system(user_input)
subprocess.call(user_input, shell=True)
eval(user_input)
```

**What to look for (PHP):**
```php
exec($input)
system($_GET['cmd'])
passthru($input)
`$input`  # backtick operator
```

**Safe alternatives:** Use array form of spawn/subprocess without shell=True; use allowlists for commands.

---

### Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
**What to look for:**
- HTTP requests where the URL is user-controlled
- Webhooks, URL preview, image fetch features
- PDF generators that fetch external URLs
- Redirects to user-supplied URLs

**High-risk targets:**
- AWS metadata service: `169.254.169.254`
- Internal services: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `10.x.x.x`, `192.168.x.x`
- Cloud metadata endpoints

**Detection:**
```js
fetch(req.body.url)
axios.get(userSuppliedUrl)
http.get(params.webhook)
```

---

## 2. Authentication & Access Control

### Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA / IDOR)
**What to look for:**
- Resource IDs taken directly from URL/params without ownership check
- `findById(req.params.id)` without verifying `userId === currentUser.id`
- Numeric sequential IDs (easily guessable)

**Example vulnerable pattern:**
```js
// VULNERABLE: no ownership check
app.get('/api/documents/:id', async (req, res) => {
  const doc = await Document.findById(req.params.id);
  res.json(doc);
});

// SAFE: verify ownership
app.get('/api/documents/:id', async (req, res) => {
  const doc = await Document.findOne({ _id: req.params.id, owner: req.user.id });
  if (!doc) return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Forbidden' });
  res.json(doc);
});
```

---

### JWT Vulnerabilities
**What to look for:**
- `alg: "none"` accepted
- Weak or hardcoded secrets: `secret`, `password`, `1234`
- No expiry (`exp` claim) validation
- Algorithm confusion (RS256 → HS256 downgrade)
- JWT stored in `localStorage` (XSS risk; prefer httpOnly cookie)

**Detection:**
```js
jwt.verify(token, secret, { algorithms: ['HS256'] })  // Check algorithms array
jwt.decode(token)  // WARNING: decode does NOT verify signature
```

---

### Missing Authentication / Authorization
**What to look for:**
- Admin or sensitive endpoints missing auth middleware
- Routes defined after `app.use(authMiddleware)` vs before it
- Feature flags or debug endpoints left exposed in production
- GraphQL resolvers missing auth checks at field level

---

### CSRF
**What to look for:**
- State-changing operations (POST/PUT/DELETE) without CSRF token
- APIs relying only on cookies for auth without SameSite attribute
- Missing `SameSite=Strict` or `SameSite=Lax` on session cookies

---

## 3. Secrets & Sensitive Data Exposure

### In-Code Secrets
Look for patterns like:
```
API_KEY = "sk-..."
password = "hunter2"
SECRET = "abc123"
private_key = "-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----"
aws_secret_access_key = "wJalrXUtn..."
```

Entropy heuristic: strings > 20 chars with high character variety in assignment context
are likely secrets even if the variable name doesn't say so.

### In Logs / Error Messages
```js
console.log('User password:', password)
logger.info({ user, token })   // token shouldn't be logged
res.status(500).json({ error: err.stack })  // stack traces expose internals
```

### Sensitive Data in API Responses
- Returning full user object including `password_hash`, `ssn`, `credit_card`
- Including internal IDs or system paths in error responses

---

## 4. Cryptography

### Weak Algorithms
| Algorithm | Issue | Replace With |
|-----------|-------|--------------|
| MD5 | Broken for security | SHA-256 or bcrypt (passwords) |
| SHA-1 | Collision attacks | SHA-256 |
| DES / 3DES | Weak key size | AES-256-GCM |
| RC4 | Broken | AES-GCM |
| ECB mode | No IV, patterns visible | GCM or CBC with random IV |

### Weak Randomness
```js
// VULNERABLE
Math.random()                    // not cryptographically secure
Date.now()                       // predictable
Math.random().toString(36)       // weak token generation

// SAFE
crypto.randomBytes(32)           // Node.js
secrets.token_urlsafe(32)        // Python
```

### Password Hashing
```python
# VULNERABLE
hashlib.md5(password.encode()).hexdigest()
hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest()

# SAFE
bcrypt.hashpw(password, bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=12))
argon2.hash(password)
```

---

## 5. Insecure Dependencies

### What to flag:
- Packages with known CVEs in installed version range
- Packages abandoned > 2 years with no security updates
- Packages with extremely broad permissions for their stated purpose
- Transitive dependencies pulling in known-bad packages
- Pinned versions that are significantly behind current (possible unpatched vulns)

### High-risk package watchlist: see `references/vulnerable-packages.md`

---

## 6. Business Logic

### Race Conditions (TOCTOU)
```js
// VULNERABLE: check then act without atomic lock
const balance = await getBalance(userId);
if (balance >= amount) {
  await deductBalance(userId, amount);  // race condition between check and deduct
}

// SAFE: use atomic DB transaction or optimistic locking
await db.transaction(async (trx) => {
  const user = await User.query(trx).forUpdate().findById(userId);
  if (user.balance < amount) throw new Error('Insufficient funds');
  await user.$query(trx).patch({ balance: user.balance - amount });
});
```

### Missing Rate Limiting
Flag endpoints that:
- Accept authentication credentials (login, 2FA)
- Send emails or SMS
- Perform expensive operations
- Expose user enumeration (password reset, registration)

---

## 7. Path Traversal
```python
# VULNERABLE
filename = request.args.get('file')
with open(f'/var/uploads/{filename}') as f:  # ../../../../etc/passwd

# SAFE
filename = os.path.basename(request.args.get('file'))
safe_path = os.path.join('/var/uploads', filename)
if not safe_path.startswith('/var/uploads/'):
    abort(400)
```

# Template: build a BSIPA mod on every push / PR.
# Place at .github/workflows/build.yml and replace MyMod with your project name.
# Reference: https://github.com/Auros/SiraUtil/blob/main/.github/workflows/build.yml
name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [master, main]
    paths:
      - "MyMod/**"
      - ".github/workflows/build.yml"
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Beat Saber references
        uses: nicoco007/setup-beat-saber@v1
        with:
          project-path: ${{ github.workspace }}\MyMod\MyMod.csproj

      - name: Verify Beat Saber references
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          if (-not $env:BeatSaberDir) { throw "BeatSaberDir is not set" }
          if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $env:BeatSaberDir "Libs"))) {
            throw "Dependency references are missing. Check DependsOn Version values and the setup-beat-saber log."
          }

      # Only needed when the project references a private NuGet feed.
      # - name: Update private NuGet source
      #   run: dotnet nuget update source "my-private-feed" --username ${{ github.actor }} --password ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} --store-password-in-clear-text

      - name: Build Release
        run: dotnet build "${{ github.workspace }}\MyMod\MyMod.csproj" -c Release

      # On GitHub Actions the BSMT template disables ZipRelease and writes
      # bin\Release\net472\Final\Plugins\MyMod.dll instead. Package that layout.
      - name: Package release zip
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $final = "MyMod\bin\Release\net472\Final"
          if (-not (Test-Path $final)) { throw "CI output not found: $final" }
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "MyMod\bin\Release\artifacts" | Out-Null
          Compress-Archive -Path "$final\*" -DestinationPath "MyMod\bin\Release\artifacts\MyMod.zip" -Force

      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: MyMod-${{ github.sha }}
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}\MyMod\bin\Release\artifacts\MyMod.zip
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

# Template: build on tag creation and attach the zip to that tag's GitHub Release.
# Place at .github/workflows/release.yml and replace MyMod with your project name.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Beat Saber references
        uses: nicoco007/setup-beat-saber@v1
        with:
          project-path: ${{ github.workspace }}\MyMod\MyMod.csproj

      - name: Verify Beat Saber references
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          if (-not $env:BeatSaberDir) { throw "BeatSaberDir is not set" }
          if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $env:BeatSaberDir "Libs"))) {
            throw "Dependency references are missing. Check DependsOn Version values and the setup-beat-saber log."
          }

      - name: Build Release
        run: dotnet build "${{ github.workspace }}\MyMod\MyMod.csproj" -c Release

      # On GitHub Actions the BSMT template disables ZipRelease and writes
      # bin\Release\net472\Final\Plugins\MyMod.dll instead. Package that layout.
      - name: Package release zip
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $final = "MyMod\bin\Release\net472\Final"
          if (-not (Test-Path $final)) { throw "CI output not found: $final" }
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "MyMod\bin\Release\artifacts" | Out-Null
          Compress-Archive -Path "$final\*" -DestinationPath "MyMod\bin\Release\artifacts\MyMod-${{ github.ref_name }}.zip" -Force

      - name: Upload workflow artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: MyMod-${{ github.ref_name }}
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}\MyMod\bin\Release\artifacts\MyMod-${{ github.ref_name }}.zip
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Attach artifacts to the tag
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          name: MyMod ${{ github.ref_name }}
          generate_release_notes: true
          prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          files: |
            MyMod/bin/Release/artifacts/MyMod-${{ github.ref_name }}.zip

# Template: build a Quest mod and release it on tag.
# Place at .github/workflows/release.yml and replace MyQuestMod with your mod name.
# Assumes the quest-mod-template layout, including .github/actions/canary-ndk.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: true
          lfs: true

      - uses: seanmiddleditch/gha-setup-ninja@v6

      - name: Setup NDK
        id: setup-ndk
        uses: ./.github/actions/canary-ndk

      - name: Create ndkpath.txt
        run: |
          echo ${{ steps.setup-ndk.outputs.ndk-path }} > ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/ndkpath.txt
          cat ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/ndkpath.txt

      - name: Setup QPM
        uses: Fernthedev/qpm-action@v1
        with:
          workflow_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          restore: true
          cache: true
          publish: false

      - name: Build QMOD
        run: |
          cd ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}
          qpm s qmod

      - name: Upload QMOD artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: MyQuestMod-${{ github.ref_name }}
          path: ./MyQuestMod.qmod
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Attach artifacts to the tag
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          name: MyQuestMod ${{ github.ref_name }}
          generate_release_notes: true
          prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          files: |
            ./MyQuestMod.qmod
